This regularity underlies the structure theory for the associated pattern-packing posets that we developed in Part I (arXiv:2610.29846). We obtain moment representations for all two-level shifted-grid families of Part I and all overlap-one patterns whose first and last letters differ by one or two. For families whose posets are trees with a unique minimum or maximum and overlap at most half the pattern length, positivity instead holds after finitely many initial terms of the enumerating sequence have been discarded. Our proofs develop further enumeration formulas and combine probabilistic constructions with total nonnegativity and weighted paths, yielding explicit laws or continued fractions in several cases. Although a previously conjectured universal moment property fails, our results establish positivity for all packing sequences associated with patterns of length at most four and all but one of the distinct sequences arising from patterns of length five. Extensive numerical evidence suggests that the remaining sequence is also a moment sequence. These results lead us to formulate refined conjectures for all overlap-one patterns and for the shifted-grid families of Part I with arbitrarily many levels.
item.dc:creator: Natasha Blitvi\'c, Mohammed Slim Kammoun, Einar Steingr\'imsson

item.title: Generalized Edge Ideals and Regularity Offset of Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.08889v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce generalized edge ideals by assigning pairwise coprime monomials, instead of variables, to the vertices of a graph. We use the lcm-lattice to show that the multigraded Betti numbers and Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of the quotient by a generalized edge ideal agree with the Betti numbers and resolution regularity of the quotient by an ordinary edge ideal in a non-standard Z-grading. We define the regularity offset as a measurement of the difference between the regularities of the quotients by a generalized edge ideal and its ordinary counterpart, and prove bounds for the regularity offset. We compute the regularity offset for co-chordal graphs and paths, and derive a formula for the regularity offset of forests. We also derive a graph-theoretic criterion for when a forest's regularity offset is always zero, or equivalently, its top-level Betti number is nonzero.
item.dc:creator: Grigoriy Blekherman, Jiaheng Li, Jianuo Zhou

item.title: The inscribed $4$-polytope of maximal volume with nine vertices
item.description: arXiv:2611.10078v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that a $4$-polytope with nine vertices inscribed in the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ has volume at most $\frac{5}{24}\sqrt{10 + 2\sqrt{5}}$, and that, up to orthogonal transformations, equality holds only for the convex hull of a square and a regular pentagon inscribed in $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ in orthogonal $2$-planes through the origin. For the combinatorial type of this polytope, whose boundary complex is the join of a $4$-cycle and a $5$-cycle, we write the signed volume as the pairing, through the Hodge star, of the area vectors of the two cycles, and bound each area vector by finite Fourier analysis; the bound holds for every choice of nine points on the sphere. Since an optimal polytope is simplicial, by a result of Horv\'ath and L\'angi, it remains to exclude the other simplicial types, which we do by sum-of-squares certificates checked in exact arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Csaba Medgyes

item.title: Discrete Spoilers: Introducing Abstract Undergraduate Mathematics Using Graph Theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.10143v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Students often have serious difficulties with many key concepts of the undergraduate mathematics curriculum. We argue that many of these difficulties can be eased by explicitly separating the key ideas from the technical details. To do so, we present finite graphs as a setting where the basic concepts appear more transparently, because on a graph most proofs only require basic techniques from linear algebra. We illustrate this approach in three areas that cover a large part of the curriculum. First, we explain basic operators from vector calculus, such as the gradient and the divergence, through the incidence matrix of a graph. Second, we show that the diffusion equation has a simple solution on a graph. We also solve the graph Dirichlet problem, in which the values at some vertices are fixed. Third, we introduce a second incidence matrix that illustrates homology, cohomology and the Helmholtz decomposition in a simple way. Finally, we outline how to apply this approach to other branches of mathematics.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Diaz-Diaz

item.title: Sharp Logarithmic-Product Bounds for List Replicability of Sign Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.10408v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: List replicability measures how many accurate hypotheses suffice to contain the output of a learning rule with arbitrarily high confidence. We prove that every nonempty class of $m$ binary concepts on $n$ domain points has list replicability at most $805\ln(2m)\ln(2n)$. This resolves the logarithmic-product conjecture of Blondal, Hatami, Hatami, Lalov, and Tretiak. Hanner matrices give lower bounds of the same order, for square matrices and for explicit families with unequal logarithmic aspect ratios. The upper bound is obtained by constructing nested acyclic sets in the faces of a cube. A critical-point estimate supplies highly connected regions, weighted cell attachments keep the sets compatible across faces, and a cubical carrier theorem converts them into accurate finite covers and learning rules. Appending one constant coordinate turns list replicability into an exact geometric quantity, the face width, and graph-orientation classes satisfy exact product formulas. In particular, there are explicit classes with list replicability $4k+1$ and equivariant index $3k$, so the additive gap between the two is unbounded. We also develop entropy-tilting and two-sided Gibbs constructions, give combinatorial upper bounds adapted to structured matrices, compute exact values on classical families, and study the index of Paley matrices.
item.dc:creator: Guangjian Zhang

item.title: A Simple Computer-Assisted Proof of the 5/6-Bound for Real-Period Pinwheel Scheduling
item.description: arXiv:2611.10624v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In pinwheel scheduling with real periods, an instance consists of $n$ tasks with real periods $1\le a_1\le a_2\le\cdots\le a_n$. The goal is to find a schedule that assigns one task to each day indefinitely such that, for every task $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ and every positive integer $\ell$, task $i$ occurs at least $\ell$ times in every block of $\lceil\ell a_i\rceil$ consecutive days. Given an instance $(a_1,a_2,\dots,a_n)$, its dimension is $n$, its density is $\sum_{i=1}^n1/a_i$, and its potential is $\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}1/a_i$. We prove that every real-valued instance of density at most 5/6 admits a periodic schedule of period length less than $4\cdot2^n$. For integer periods, the 5/6 density bound was a long-standing conjecture settled by Kawamura using a computer-assisted proof [STOC 2024, PNAS 2026]. Our result confirms the real-period conjecture of Fujiwara, Miyagi, and Ouchi [DMTCS 2026]. Our computer-assisted proof builds on Kawamura's ideas while using fewer explicit schedules. It combines dimension reduction by folding with nine satisfiability modulo theories (SMT) checks over linear real arithmetic. A set of 14287 explicit periodic schedules contains a schedule for every instance of dimension at most 8 and density at most 5/6, and for every instance of dimension 9 and potential at most 5/6. Folding is used to reduce every instance of larger dimension and potential at most 5/6 to an instance of dimension 9 and the same potential bound. We also prove that every real-valued instance with minimum period at least 4 and density at most 17/20=0.85 admits a periodic schedule of period length less than $19\cdot2^n$. The density bound 17/20 is tight and improves the 0.84-bound of Mishra, Rho, and Kleinberg [arXiv 2025] for integer periods. It also resolves the $a_1=4$ case of Kawamura's 2025 conjecture that integer-valued instances of density at most $1-(a_1-1)/(a_1(a_1+1))$ are schedulable.
item.dc:creator: Hiroshi Fujiwara, Grzegorz Gutowski, Katsuhisa Ouchi, Alexander Wolff

item.title: Automorphism of reduced finitary power monoids
item.description: arXiv:2611.10645v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $H$ be a multiplicatively written monoid with identity element $1_H$. The family $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},1}(H)$ of all finite subsets of $H$ containing $1_H$ is a monoid with identity $\{1_H\}$ under the setwise multiplication induced by $H$. We prove that $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},1}(H)) \cong \operatorname{Aut}(H)$ whenever $H$ satisfies either of the following two conditions: (1) $H$ is commutative, cancellative, and contains an invertible element of infinite order; (2) $H$ is an abelian group which is not isomorphic to the Klein four-group.
item.dc:creator: Yongjie Peng, Guixin Deng

item.title: Weighted Matroid Intersection under Minimum Rank Oracle
item.description: arXiv:2611.10701v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider matroid intersection under the minimum rank oracle model, in which two matroids are accessible only through an oracle that returns the minimum of the ranks of a given set in the two matroids. By Edmonds' theorem, this oracle determines the matroid intersection polytope, although it does not reveal the exchangeability graphs on which classical algorithms rely. Recent work by B\'ar\'asz, B\'erczi, Kir\'aly, Oki, Yamaguchi, and Yokoi (2025) showed that unweighted matroid intersection is polynomially solvable in this model. In this paper, we present a strongly polynomial-time algorithm for weighted matroid intersection in this model. The key to our algorithm is a polynomial-size extended formulation of tangent cones of common base polytopes that can be constructed using the minimum rank oracle. We also give min-max theorems in terms of the minimum rank function via 1/3-submodularity, and present a strongly polynomial-time algorithm to compute an optimal dual solution.
item.dc:creator: Taihei Oki

item.title: Optimal rational spherical designs on the circle
item.description: arXiv:2611.10702v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The minimum numbers of points in rational equal-weight spherical designs on the circle are $2304$, $4608$, $9216$, and $9216$ at strengths $4$, $5$, $6$, and $7$, respectively. We construct two nonisometric optimal designs at each strength. At arbitrary strength $t$, we obtain an explicit cardinality divisor $D_t$ with $\log D_t=(1/2+o(1))t\log t$. Applied to the antipodal pairs of a $4608$-point design, Gromov's torus construction gives a flat minimal immersion of $\mathbb{T}^2$ into $S^{4607}$ with $2304$ distinct integral frequencies, attaining Petrunin's sharp Euclidean normal-curvature bound.
item.dc:creator: Zhuo Cheng, Yeyao Hu, Deyu Yu

item.title: Linear structure graphs associated with commuting graphs of Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.10788v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The commuting graph (CG) of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field of characteristic zero forgets the linear structure, and a non-trivial center creates redundant vertices. We introduce linear structure graphs (LSGs), whose vertices are the nonzero vectors of a vector space and whose edge set is stable under linear operations. Each vertex generates a finite ascending sequence of subspaces, which defines its LSG-depth; this depth governs connectivity. We characterize LSGs of depth at most 1 and show that the CG of a Lie algebra with trivial center has depth at most 1 if and only if the algebra is a commutative transitive Lie algebra (CTLA). The reduced commuting graph (RCG) restricts the CG to a complement of the center; it is well defined up to LSG-isomorphism, preserves the connectivity, diameter and number of components of the CG, and is compatible with direct sums. Finally, we characterize almost abelian Lie algebras (AALAs) by their RCGs.
item.dc:creator: Vu A. Le, Hoa Q. Duong, Tuan A. Nguyen

item.title: An explicit basis for the unipotent Specht modules of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.10813v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For each partition $\lambda$ of $n$ we construct an explicit basis of the unipotent Specht module $S^\lambda$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, defined recursively over horizontal strips. Each basis vector is $g\,x_\tau$, where $\tau$ is a semistandard tableau of shape $\lambda$, $x_\tau$ is obtained from a Steinberg-type vector by alternately applying a permutation matrix and a Fourier sum over a unitriangular group, and $g$ runs over an explicit set of coset representatives. Grouping the basis by the standardization of $\tau$ gives exactly $q^{\mathrm{maj}(s^T)}$ vectors for each standard tableau $s$, which is the numerical form of the Dipper-James standard basis problem. The same family is a basis over every field containing a nontrivial $p$th root of unity, including fields whose characteristic divides $|\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)|$, and a subfamily chosen layer by layer gives a basis of the simple quotient $D^\lambda$. We also give a basis of the $U$-fixed vectors of $S^\lambda$ and computed values of $\dim D^\lambda$ for $\mathrm{GL}_n(2)$.
item.dc:creator: Scott Andrews

item.title: Quantum channel bounds for constant-composition codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.10827v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend the quantum-channel optimization of Alrabiah and Guruswami to $q$-ary constant-composition codes. We study explicit channel and flag constructions that recover selected classical asymptotic upper bounds, including the Ben-Haim--Litsyn, moving-subspace and Horn-channel bounds. We give two equivalent formulations, Gram and flag, and prove stability of the obtained upper bounds under permutation transport and generalized shortening. A hierarchy defined by bounding the output-state ranks within each flag improves strictly between consecutive levels at every composition and every positive distance below the Plotkin threshold. We provide finite matrix parametrizations of these bounds (i.e., the number of variables does not depend on the length of codes under consideration). Numerical optimization rapidly produces improvements over the known asymptotic upper bounds throughout all tested nonbinary parameter ranges. For rational input data, each finite level admits near-optimal feasible rational descriptions of polynomial length. Their feasibility can be checked exactly and their objective values computed to any prescribed accuracy in polynomial time; the associated threshold problem with a prescribed gap belongs to $\mathsf{PromiseNP}$.
item.dc:creator: Artur Akhiiarov, Peter Boyvalenkov, Danila Cherkashin, Andrei Raigorodskii

item.title: New lower bounds for even and odd values of the partition function
item.description: arXiv:2611.10899v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)$ and $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)$ denote the numbers of integers $0\leq n< X$ for which the ordinary partition function $p(n)$ is odd and even, respectively. The Parkin--Shanks conjecture predicts that $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)$ and $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)$ are both asymptotic to $X/2$. Bella\"iche and Nicolas proved that $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)\gg \sqrt{X} \log \log X$, while Zheng, building on work of Ono and Swaminathan, recently proved that $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)\gg \sqrt{X}$. We improve both bounds simultaneously by proving $\min\{N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X), N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)\}\gg X^{3/4}/(\log X \log \log X)$.
item.dc:creator: Liuquan Wang

item.title: Spectral gaps and mixing rates of primitive matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.10951v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We obtain lower bounds on spectral gap/upper bounds for mixing rate for arbitrary $n$-state (not necessarily reversible) primitive Markov chains which have exponent $-O(n)$ rather than $-O(n^2)$, a significant improvement on the order obtained from classical arguments. Our improvements come from using the irreducibility distance and chainable index (which are at most linear in $n$) rather than the primitivity index (which can be near $n^2$). This also yields corresponding bounds for arbitrary nonnegative primitive matrices.
item.dc:creator: Solly Coles, Ronnie Pavlov

item.title: The Herzog--Sch\"onheim Conjecture for Solvable Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.11002v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Herzog--Sch\"onheim conjecture states that if a group is partitioned into finitely many, and at least two, cosets of subgroups, then two of these subgroups have the same index. We prove the conjecture for all solvable groups, finite or infinite. Sun's bound on unions of cosets, applied in a quotient, is combined with divisibility restrictions on local indices relative to the subgroup generated by the $p$-elements, where $p$ is the largest prime divisor of the order of a minimal counterexample. These restrictions are obtained by counting fixed points in a primitive solvable quotient. This suffices except at the prime $7$, where the counting bound narrowly fails and an additional overlap argument is needed. The proof has been formalized in Lean~4 with mathlib.
item.dc:creator: Murali Menon

item.title: Statistics of centralizers of integer matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.11287v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: With recent interests on the statistics of commuting integer matrices, we study the related problem on the statistics of the set of centralizer of a matrix. We provide asymptotics and bounds on the size of such set when restricted to integer matrices of bounded height.
item.dc:creator: Muhammad Afifurrahman, Wildan Bagus Wicaksono

item.title: Linear Objective Problems: A Complexity Framework for Bilevel Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.11375v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many bilevel and robust optimization problems are complete for the second level of the polynomial hierarchy, but such results are usually proven one problem at a time with problem-specific reductions. A recurring obstacle is that the lower level must select an optimal solution rather than merely a feasible one, whereas standard reductions preserve only whether a solution exists, not which solutions are optimal. We introduce linear objective problems (LOP), a framework for optimization problems whose solutions are explicit subsets of a ground set and whose objective is linear in these elements. We define tight solution-embedding reductions, which map the optimal solutions of one problem element by element onto the optimal solutions of another, without having to recognize optimal solutions, which is coNP-hard in general. This gives a notion of LOP-completeness, with Satisfiability as the canonical complete problem, even with unit weights. We show that many classical problems are LOP-complete, including Vertex Cover, Dominating Set, TSP, Knapsack, and Steiner Tree, and we introduce a duality that transfers LOP-completeness between minimization and maximization problems. As our main application, we prove a meta-theorem for min-max regret optimization under interval uncertainty: for every LOP-complete problem, the min-max regret version is $\Sigma_2^p$-complete. Instead of a separate proof for each nominal problem, it suffices to show that the nominal problem is LOP-complete. This recovers known results for the interval min-max regret versions of Knapsack and Maximum Benefit Set Cover and yields completeness for over 50 further problems.
item.dc:creator: Christoph Gr\"une, James B. Orlin, Lasse Wulf

item.title: On the Complexity of Extending Prescribed Linear Forests to Hamiltonian Cycles in Hypercubes
item.description: arXiv:2611.11476v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube, and let $P\subseteq E(Q_n)$ be a set of prescribed edges. It is known that, for $n\ge 2$, every such set $P$ with $|P|\leq 2n-3$ whose edges form a linear forest is contained in a Hamiltonian cycle of $Q_n$. This bound is sharp for general linear forests. The computational complexity of deciding whether a prescribed edge set of a hypercube can be extended to a Hamiltonian cycle was posed as an open question by Dvo\v{r}\'ak [SIAM J. Discrete Math. 19 (2005) 135--144]. We prove that the problem is NP-complete even when the prescribed edges form a spanning linear forest with no isolated vertices. We give a polynomial-time reduction from a restricted 3-SAT problem, using local spanning path-forest gadgets for variables and clauses that are uniformly embedded in the hypercube. The same reduction therefore establishes NP-hardness of two versions of Hamiltonian-cycle extension problems for general prescribed edge sets.
item.dc:creator: Huazhong L\"{u}, Tingzeng Wu

item.title: Induced-Minor-Free Graphs Admit a Star-Based Separator of Size $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{n})$
item.description: arXiv:2611.11513v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given an $H$-induced-minor-free graph $G$ with $n$ vertices, we construct a balanced separator of $G$ consisting of $\tilde{O}(|V(H)|\sqrt{n})$ star subgraphs. Our result is an induced-minor-free analog of the famous separator theorem for $H$-minor-free graphs by Alon, Seymour, and Thomas [J. Amer. Math. Soc., 1990]. A key idea in our construction is a new decomposition of $H$-induced-minor-free graphs, analogous to the cop decomposition for $H$-minor-free graphs by Andreae [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B, 1986]. We also discuss several algorithmic applications of our result.
item.dc:creator: Arnold Filtser, Nikolai Karol, Hung Le, Florian Lehner

item.title: Infinite sumsets via model theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.11543v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove versions of (variations of) Erd\H{o}s sumset and $B+B+t$ conjectures asked by Kra, Moreira, Richter and Robertson for semigroups equipped with pairwise commuting non-algebraic definable Keisler measures. Our results use model-theoretic methods involving the existence of \emph{many} coheir independent tuples in every definable relation of positive density.
item.dc:creator: Amador Martin-Pizarro, Daniel Palac\'in

item.title: On sinks and mirrors
item.description: arXiv:2611.11660v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a full rank sink recurrent cluster $\mathcal{A}$ variety, we prove that its wrapped Fukaya category is equivalent to the category of coherent sheaves on a stacky elaboration of the dual Fock-Goncharov cluster $\mathcal{X}$ variety. In particular, braid varieties for a semisimple group are mirror to the braid varieties for the Langlands dual group. Another example: for compact surfaces with no interior marked points, a least one marked point on each boundary component, and at least two marked points in total, the Fock-Goncharov moduli for SL(2) and PGL(2) are homologically mirror. The results were obtained in communion with ChatGPT Astra.
item.dc:creator: Mingyuan Hu, Vivek Shende

item.title: The cohomology of finite simple groups is unbounded
item.description: arXiv:2611.11677v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In every fixed positive degree, we show that the cohomology of finite simple groups, algebraic groups and quantum groups, with coefficients in simple modules, can have arbitrarily large dimension. In particular, we disprove Guralnick's conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Chris Bowman, Damian de la Fuente, Nicolas Libedinsky, David Plaza

item.title: Frobenius and ozone automorphism groups of root of unity quantum cluster algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.11699v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many important families of algebras $R$ in the areas of quantum groups, quantum topology and noncommutative algebra are root of unity quantum algebras, equipped with Frobenius centers $Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R) \subseteq Z(R)$ and quantum Frobenius maps ${\mathrm{Fr}} : R_{\mathrm{class}} \stackrel{\cong}{\longrightarrow} Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R)$. We explicitly classify the Frobenius automorphism groups ${\mathrm{Aut}}(R/Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R))$ and the ozone groups ${\mathrm{Oz}}(R):= {\mathrm{Aut}}(R/Z(R))$, and prove that all endomorphisms of $R$ fixing its Frobenius center $Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R)$ are automorphisms for all algebras $R$ that come from partial root of unity quantum cluster and upper quantum cluster algebras (which have been proved to encompass a vast majority of known quantum algebras). We prove three main theorems that give the above classification results from three different standpoints. As applications, we classify the Frobenius and ozone automorphism groups of all quantum function algebras of simple algebraic groups $G$ not of type $F_4$ or $E_8$ and all quantum unipotent cells at roots of unity for arbitrary symmetrizable Kac--Moody algebras.
item.dc:creator: Yunmeng Wu, Milen Yakimov

item.title: Binary Belief Propagation Fixed Points: Finiteness, Rigidity, and Topological Complexity
item.description: arXiv:2611.11713v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A fixed finite binary Ising model has only finitely many admissible complex belief propagation fixed points, even at degenerate parameter values. Families of positive fixed points obtained by varying external fields can nevertheless have nontrivial topology. We study this distinction through the external-field projection. For a fixed field, we prove finiteness by bounding the pole orders of the magnetizations on a hypothetical complex solution curve. The generic degree on the support graph then bounds the total local multiplicity. A graph has a single smooth real line as its full positive response for every choice of positive couplings, base field, and strictly positive sweep direction exactly when it contains no two vertex-disjoint connected subgraphs of cycle rank at least two. Two such subgraphs suffice to create a circular component. For a plane obtained by varying two vertex fields, connected simple bipartite cubic graphs with one uniform coupling and a universal bound on the fixed fields realize every genus. The minimum number of vertices grows logarithmically in the genus, by a matching algebraic upper bound on Betti numbers. Finally, we certify the complete field discriminant of an eighteen-vertex product model and recover its torus component's genus from the counts of distinct roots on all field cells. The three main theorems, including the logarithmic size bounds, are formally verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib.
item.dc:creator: Yusuke Watanabe

item.title: Probabilistic counting of labelled trees with prescribed vertical edge profile
item.description: arXiv:2611.12525v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The vertical edge profile of a labelled plane tree $t$ is the collection of integers counting the number of oriented edges from label $i$ to label $j$ for every possible pairs of labels $(i, j)$. In a previous work by the second author, it was shown that a process constructed from the vertical edge profile forms a Markov chain for a wide class of models of random labelled plane trees where edge label increments are constrained to lie in $\{-1, 0, 1\}$. The purpose of this paper is twofold. First, we continue the study of Markov properties of the vertical edge profile. In particular, we derive general formulas for the transition kernel and the initial distribution of a class of Markov chains related to the vertical edge profile. Second, we apply these results to the probabilistic enumeration of trees with a prescribed vertical edge profile. These applications yield a unified probabilistic derivation of several enumeration formulas. In particular, we recover some results established Bousquet-M\'elou and Chapuy for binary trees and Cayley trees. These enumeration formulas admit a remarkable factorized form, already noted in previous works. The probabilistic methods developed here explain this phenomenon by showing that these factorizations arise naturally from the Markov structure underlying the vertical edge profile.
item.dc:creator: Vanessa Dan, Alexis Metz-Donnadieu

item.title: Counter-examples to Conjectures on NCCRs via a Reductive McKay Correspondence
item.description: arXiv:2611.12679v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We disprove three conjectures appearing in Van den Bergh's plenary ICM survey, posed by De Deyn and Van den Bergh, which concern the interplay between non-commutative crepant resolutions (NCCRs) and the stringy Euler characteristic. Our counter-examples are applications of a new McKay correspondence for reductive groups that we prove in this paper, extending the classical McKay correspondence for finite groups. We obtain explicit formulas for the stringy $E$-functions of reductive quotients in terms of the Weyl group action and stringy $E$-functions of toric varieties; we also obtain an equivalent formula expressed as an integral of the age function over Weyl-fixed loci of a compact real torus. For symmetric representations, our expressions are related to arithmetic Tutte polynomials, yielding combinatorial formulas for the stringy Euler characteristic.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Satriano, Jeremy Usatine

item.title: Functorial Homological Mirror Symmetry for Acyclic Cluster Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.12751v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce the formalism of cluster models, a class of log Calabi-Yau varieties obtained from smooth quasi-affine toric varieties by iterated affine blowups along non-toric codimension 2 centers determined by a really full rank quiver. Cluster models include the truncated cluster varieties of Gross, Hacking, and Keel with respect to really full rank quivers, all really full rank acyclic cluster varieties, and all open toric subvarieties of $\mathbb{C}^n\times(\mathbb{C}^*)^m$. We then construct mirrors to cluster models via iterated Weinstein handle attachments to toric mirrors, so that the corresponding skeleta acquire compact pieces, and we prove homological mirror symmetry for all cluster models, compatibly with freezing, deleting, and contracting vertices of the quiver. This extends toric mirror symmetry and its naturalities beyond the cotangent bundle. In particular, we obtain homological mirror symmetry for all really full rank acyclic cluster varieties. We develop this package with a view towards conjectures of Marsh, Rietsch, and Williams about mirror symmetry for Grassmannians and closed positroid varieties. Motivated by these, we also conjecture that open positroid varieties are self-mirror. Assuming a natural ansatz, we prove this for a class of positroid varieties that includes nontrivial cells in every Grassmannian and all cells in finite-type Grassmannians. Towards this end we introduce a new combinatorial input, the notion of weak $k$-booleanness for permutations and braids.
item.dc:creator: Josephine Hlavinka

item.title: The finite volume method on Sierpi\'nski simplices
item.description: arXiv:1806.04531v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the sequel, we extend the Strichartz average approach for the Laplacian, which uses average values of a function over basic sets, rather than pointwise ones as classically done in the literature, and goes back to the seminal work of~S.~Kusuoka and~X.~Y.~Zhou, to Sierpi\'{n}ski Simplices. To our knowledge, the finite volume method had not been applied before to fractals themselves, with their intrinsic Laplacian. We build the finite volume scheme for the heat equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions, give its consistency error, a stability condition of Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy type, obtained by means of an inclusion between the spectrum of the finite volume matrix and the one of the graph Laplacian, and prove the convergence of the scheme. Numerical results are given in the case of the Sierpi\'{n}ski Gasket and Tetrahedron, and compared with the finite difference method.
item.dc:creator: Nizare Riane, Claire David

item.title: Tiling an Equilateral Triangle
item.description: arXiv:1812.07014v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $ABC$ be an equilateral triangle. For certain triangles $T$ (the ``tile'') and certain $N$, it is possible to cut $ABC$ into $N$ copies of $T$. It is known that only certain shapes of $T$ are possible, but until now very little was known about the possible values of $N$. Here we prove that for $N>3$, $N$ cannot be prime, and study more closely the possible tilings when the tile has a $\pi/3$ angle. All theorems have been formalized in Lean.
item.dc:creator: Michael Beeson

item.title: Ratio of tiling generating functions of semi-hexagons and quartered hexagons with dents
item.description: arXiv:2006.10900v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the tiling generating functions of semi-hexagons and quartered hexagons with dents on their sides. In general, there are no simple product formulas for these generating functions. However, we show that the modification in the regions' width changes the tiling generating functions by only a simple multiplicative factor.
item.dc:creator: Tri Lai

item.title: Calligraphs and sphere realizations
item.description: arXiv:2308.15305v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a recursive procedure for computing the number of realizations of a minimally rigid graph on the sphere up to rotations. We accomplish this by combining two ingredients. The first is a framework that allows us to think of such realizations as of elements of a moduli space of stable rational curves with marked points. The second is the idea of splitting a minimally rigid graph into two subgraphs, called calligraphs, that admit one degree of freedom and that share only a single edge and a further vertex. This idea has been recently employed for realizations of graphs in the plane up to isometries. The key result is that we can associate to a calligraph a triple of natural numbers with a special property: whenever a minimally rigid graph is split into two calligraphs, the number of realizations of the former equals the product of the two triples of the latter, where this product is specified by a fixed quadratic form. These triples and quadratic form codify the fact that we express realizations as intersections of two curves on the blowup of a sphere along two pairs of complex conjugate points.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Gallet, Georg Grasegger, Niels Lubbes, Josef Schicho

item.title: Orbit structures and complexity in Schubert and Richardson Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2405.13774v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The goal of this paper is twofold. Firstly, we provide a type-uniform formula for the torus complexity of the usual torus action on a Richardson variety, by developing the notion of algebraic dimensions of Bruhat intervals, strengthening a type $A$ result by Donten-Bury, Escobar and Portakal. In the process, we give an explicit description of the torus action on any Deodhar component as well as describe the root subgroups that comprise the component. Secondly, when a Levi subgroup in a reductive algebraic group acts on a Schubert variety, we exhibit a codimension preserving bijection between the Levi-Borel subgroup (a Borel subgroup in the Levi subgroup) orbits in the big open cell of that Schubert variety and torus orbits in the big open cell of a distinguished Schubert subvariety. This bijection has many applications including a type-uniform formula for the Levi-Borel complexity of the usual Levi-Borel subgroup action on a Schubert variety. We conclude by extending the Levi-Borel complexity results to a large class of Schubert varieties in the partial flag variety.
item.dc:creator: Yibo Gao, Reuven Hodges

item.title: Explicit expressions for iterates of power series
item.description: arXiv:2409.09809v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present several formulas for both the discrete and fractional iterates of an invertible power series $f,$ using a new unifying approach based on umbral calculus. Known formulas are extended, and their proofs simplified, while new expressions are introduced. In particular, by employing $q$-calculus identities, we eliminate the requirement for $f'(0)$ to equal $1$ and the resulting general expressions for the iterative logarithm are also obtained.
item.dc:creator: Kei Beauduin

item.title: The Maximum Number of Sets for 12 Cards is 14
item.description: arXiv:2501.12565v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyze a mathematical property of the popular card game SET. We present a revised geometric and computer-assisted proof that the maximum number of sets for 12 cards is 14 using finite field geometry, combinatorics, and graph theory. We present several computer algorithms for finding or approximating the maximum number of sets. We show a complete computer proof that iterates over all possible board configurations. We use this method to compute the maximum number of sets with 4 properties for a small number of cards, but it is generally too inefficient. With this method, we compute the maximum number of sets for 3 properties for all possible numbers of cards. Finally, we compare this to an existing approximation algorithm for finding maximal sets.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: 2025 IEEE Conference on Games (CoG), Lisbon, Portugal, 2025
item.dc:creator: Justin Stevens, Duncan Wilson, Richard Kelley

item.title: On the distance signless Laplacian spectral radius, fractional matching and factors of graphs
item.description: arXiv:2505.13863v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The distance signless Laplacian matrix of a graph $G$ is define as $Q(G)=$Tr$(G)+D(G)$, where Tr$(G)$ and $D(G)$ are the diagonal matrix of vertex transmissions and the distance matrix of $G$, respectively. Denote by $E_G(v)$ the set of all edges incident to a vertex $v$ in $G$. A fractional matching of a graph $G$ is a function $f:E(G) \rightarrow [0,1]$ such that $\sum_{e\in E_G(v)} f(e)\leq 1$ for every vertex $v\in V(G)$. The fractional matching number $\mu_f(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the maximum value of $ \sum_{e\in E(G)} f(e)$ over all fractional matchings. Given subgraphs $H_1, H_2,...,H_k$ of $G$, a $\{H_1, H_2,...,H_k\}$-factor of $G$ is a spanning subgraph $F$ in which each connected component is isomorphic to one of $H_1, H_2,...,H_k$. In this paper, we establish a upper bound for the distance signless Laplacian spectral radius of a graph $G$ of order $n$ to guarantee that $\mu_f(G)> \frac{n-k}{2}$, where $1\leq k<n$ is an integer. Besides, we also provide a sufficient condition based on distance signless Laplacian spectral radius to guarantee the existence of a $\{K_2,\{C_k\}\}$-factor in a graph, where $k \geq 3$ is an integer.
item.dc:creator: Zhenhao Zhang, Ligong Wang

item.title: Colorful circuits and colorful topes in oriented matroids
item.description: arXiv:2509.13718v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide a short proof of a conic version of the colorful Carath\'{e}odory theorem for oriented matroids. Holmsen's extension of the colorful Carath\'{e}odory theorem to oriented matroids (Advances in Mathematics, 2016) already encompasses several generalizations of the original result, but not its conic version. Our approach relies on a common generalization of Sperner's lemma and Meshulam's lemma - two closely related results from combinatorial topology that have found a number of applications in discrete geometry and combinatorics. This generalization may be of independent interest. Using a similar approach, we also establish the following colorful theorem for topes, whose special geometric case had not been considered before: Given $n$ topes from a uniform oriented matroid with $n$ elements, if they agree on some element, then there is a way to select a distinct element from each tope, together with its sign, so as to form another tope of the oriented matroid. Motivated by this theorem, we further explore other conditions leading to the same conclusion.
item.dc:creator: Minho Cho, Seunghun Lee, Fr\'ed\'eric Meunier

item.title: Vu's conjecture holds for claw-free graphs
item.description: arXiv:2510.15553v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a graph $G$, let $\Delta_2(G)$ denote the maximum number of neighbors any two distinct vertices of $G$ have in common. Vu (2002) proposed that, provided $\Delta_2(G)$ is not too small as a proportion of the maximum degree $\Delta(G)$ of $G$, the chromatic number of $G$ should never be too much larger than $\Delta_2(G)$. We make a first approach towards Vu's conjecture from a structural graph theoretic point of view. We prove that, in the case where $G$ is claw-free, indeed the chromatic number of $G$ is at most $\Delta_2(G)+3$. This is tight, as our bound is met with equality for the line graph of the Petersen graph. Moreover, we can prove this in terms of the more specific parameter that bounds the maximum number of neighbors any two endpoints of some edge of $G$ have in common. Our result may be viewed as a generalization of the classic bound of Vizing (1964) for edge-coloring.
item.dc:creator: Linda Cook, Ross J. Kang, Eileen Robinson, Gabri\"elle Zwaneveld

item.title: Bounded ratios for Lorentzian matrices
item.description: arXiv:2510.25030v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study multiplicative inequalities among entries of Lorentzian matrices, referred to as bounded ratios. These inequalities can be viewed as generalizations of the classical Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for mixed volumes. Our main structural result identifies the cone of all bounded ratios on Lorentzian matrices with the dual of the cut cone, a finitely generated integral polyhedral cone extensively studied in metric geometry and graph theory. We examine in detail the pentagonal ratio, which first appears for Lorentzian matrices of size at least five. For Lorentzian matrices of size three, we determine the optimal bounding constants across the entire cone of bounded ratios, obtaining an explicit entropy-like formula.
item.dc:creator: Daoji Huang, June Huh, Daniel Soskin, Botong Wang

item.title: Emerging consecutive pattern avoidance
item.description: arXiv:2511.02442v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this note we study the asymptotic popularity, that is, the limit probability to find a given consecutive pattern at a random position in a random permutation in the eighteen classes of permutations avoiding at least two length 3 consecutive patterns. We show that for ten classes, this popularity can be readily deduced from the structure of the permutations. By combining analytical and bijective approaches, we study in detail two more involved cases. The problem remains open for five classes.
item.dc:creator: Nathana\"el Hassler, Sergey Kirgizov

item.title: Effective Resistance in Simplicial Complexes: Generalizations and Properties
item.description: arXiv:2511.10749v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Originally introduced in circuit theory, the notion of effective resistance has been fruitfully exploited in graph theory, where each edge in a graph is understood as a resistor in an electric network. In this context, the effective resistance between two vertices quantifies the total opposition to current flow when a unit current is injected at one vertex and extracted at the other. As such, it encodes rich structural and geometric information about the underlying graph: it satisfies a minimum-energy principle termed Thomson's principle, defines a metric on the vertex set, relates to the topology of the graph through Foster's theorem, and determines the probability of appearance of an edge in a random spanning tree. Generalizations of effective resistance to simplicial complexes have been proposed in several forms, often formulated as matrix products of standard operators associated with the complex. We introduce a novel, basis-independent bilinear form, derived from an algebraic reinterpretation of circuit theory, that extends the classical effective resistance from graphs to simplicial complexes. This bilinear form acts on chains and cochains, and in particular, simplices and cosimplices in a simplicial complex. Our framework subsumes and unifies all existing matrix-based formulations of effective resistance. Moreover, we establish higher-order analogues of several fundamental properties known in the graph case: (i) we extend Thomson's principle to our basis-free framework; (ii) we establish metric properties for the effective resistance and its square root on chains and cycles, recovering the classical graph case; (iii) we provide a generalization of Foster's theorem to simplicial complexes; and (iv) we prove a matrix-tree theorem for higher-dimensional spanning trees, linking effective resistance to the probability of appearance of a simplex in random simplicial spanning trees.
item.dc:creator: In\'es Garc\'ia-Redondo, Claudia Landi, Sarah Percival, Anda Skeja, Bei Wang, Ling Zhou

item.title: On two conjectures in spectral hypergraph theory
item.description: arXiv:2601.04514v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a connected uniform hypergraph $H$, we prove two conjectures concerning the algebraic multiplicities of the spectral radius of its adjacency tensor and the zero eigenvalue of its Laplacian tensor. In particular, we establish that the algebraic multiplicity of each of these eigenvalues is equal to the cardinality of the corresponding projective eigenvariety.
item.dc:creator: Ya-Nan Zheng

item.title: Efficient total facial coloring of combinatorial maps
item.description: arXiv:2601.12514v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $1<k\in\mathbb{Z}$. A total coloring of a connected simple regular graph $G$ via color set $]k]_0=\{0,1,\ldots, k\}$ is efficient if each color yields an efficient dominating set, where efficient domination applies to each color class in $V(G)$. An efficient total coloring of $G$ via $[k]_0$ extends to an efficient total facial coloring $c$ of a map $M(G)$ of $G$ if it assigns a vertex-and-edge $k$-color set to the boundary cycle of each face, with the consequently missing color assigned to the face itself, so that the two adjacent faces along each edge are assigned different colors. Focus is set upon planar and toroidal maps. Modifications of $c$ are also treated by removing a perfect dominating set or a 1-factor from $G$.
item.dc:creator: Italo J. Dejter

item.title: Size conditions and spectral conditions for generalized factor-critical (bicritical) graphs and $k$-$d$-critical graphs
item.description: arXiv:2602.01512v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mbox{odd}(G)$ and $i(G)$ denote the number of nontrivial odd components and the number of isolated vertices of a graph $G$, respectively. The $k$-Berge-Tutte-formula of a graph $G$ is defined as: $\mbox{def}_k(G)=\mathop{\text{max}}\limits_{S\subseteq V(G)}\{k\cdot i(G-S)-k|S|\} $ for even $k$; $\mbox{def}_k(G)=\mathop{\mbox{max}}\limits_{S\subseteq V(G)}\{\mbox{odd}(G-S)+k\cdot i(G-S)-k|S|\} $ for odd $k$. A $k$-barrier of a graph $G$ is the subset $S\subseteq V(G)$ that reaches the maximum value in the $k$-Berge-Tutte-formula of $G$. A graph $G$ of odd order (resp. even order) is generalized factor-critical (resp. generalized bicritical) if $\emptyset$ is its only $k$-barrier. Denote by $E_G(v)$ the set of all edges incident to a vertex $v$ in $G$. A $k$-matching of a graph $G$ is a function $f:E(G) \rightarrow \{0,1,...,k\}$ such that $\sum_{e\in E_G(v)} f(e)$ $\leq k$ for every vertex $v\in V(G)$. For $1\leq d\leq k$ and $d \equiv |V(G)|$(mod 2), if for any $ v \in V(G)$, there exists a $k$-matching $f$ such that $\sum_{e\in E_G(v)}f(e)=k-d$ and $\sum_{e\in E_G(u)}f(e)=k \text{ for any } u\in V(G)-\{v\}$. Then $G$ is $k$-$d$-critical. In this paper, we establish tight sufficient conditions in terms of size or spectral radius respectively for a graph $G$ to be generalized factor-critical, generalized bicritical, and $k$-$d$-critical. Furthermore, we prove the equivalence of the existence of four factors (namely, $\{K_2,\{C_t: t\geq 3\}\}$-factor, $\{K_2,\{C_{2t+1}:t\geq 1 \}\}$-factor, fractional perfect matching, perfect $k$-matching with even $k$) in a graph. Thus we also give size conditions and spectral radius conditions for a graph $G-v$ to have one of the four factors for any $v\in V(G)$.
item.dc:creator: Zhenhao Zhang, Ligong Wang

item.title: Induced Cycles of Many Lengths
item.description: arXiv:2602.06874v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be a graph and let $\mathrm{cl}(G)$ be the number of distinct induced cycle lengths in $G$. We show that for $c,t\in \mathbb N$, every graph $G$ that does not contain an induced subgraph isomorphic to $K_{t+1}$ or $K_{t,t}$ and satisfies $\mathrm{cl}(G) \le c$ has bounded treewidth. As a consequence, we obtain a polynomial-time algorithm for deciding whether a graph $G$ contains induced cycles of at least three distinct lengths.
item.dc:creator: Maria Chudnovsky, Ilya Maier

item.title: The permutation automorphism groups of irreducible cyclic codes
item.description: arXiv:2603.01904v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The study of permutation automorphism groups of cyclic codes is a central topic in algebraic coding theory. A cyclic code over $\mathbb{F}_q$ is called irreducible if its check polynomial is irreducible over $\mathbb{F}_q$, and it is non-degenerate if it is not periodic. Such a non-degenerate code is standard if its permutation automorphism group is equal to the group generated by the cyclic shift and the Frobenius automorphism, and non-standard otherwise. In this paper, we give a complete classification of all non-standard non-degenerate irreducible cyclic codes, using the classification of finite simple groups. Our result shows that, apart from a small number of explicit exceptional families and their descendants under certain secondary constructions, every non-degenerate irreducible cyclic code is standard, and up to four explicit exceptions, every nonzero degenerate cyclic code is non-standard. This classification has several consequences. First, it yields a general description of non-standard linear recurring sequence subgroups, extending the earlier work of Brison and Nogueira; secondly, it establishes the Schmidt-White conjecture for all non-standard non-degenerate irreducible cyclic codes. Moreover, our results provide strong evidence in support of the conjecture of Berger and Charpin that almost all cyclic codes are standard.
item.dc:creator: Tao Feng, Henk D. L. Hollmann, Weicong Li, Qing Xiang

item.title: Mutation of Theta Functions
item.description: arXiv:2603.19391v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give an account of mutation of theta functions in cluster scattering diagrams, starting with a notion of mutation that is related to, but different from, the notion of mutation defined by Gross, Hacking, Keel, and Kontsevich.This different approach to mutation leads to several applications. Three of the applications simplify the process of computing structure constants for multiplication of theta functions, and these are used in another paper on cluster scattering diagrams of affine type. Notable in these three applications is the appearance of mutation symmetries and dominance regions. The other two applications have to do with pointed reduced bases, a variation on the pointed bases of Fan Qin. We give a characterization of pointed reduced bases analogous to Qin's characterization of pointed bases. All of these applications take place in a version of Gross, Hacking, Keel, and Kontsevich's canonical algebra that can be constructed for an arbitrary exchange matrix.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Reading, Salvatore Stella

item.title: Negative Avoiding Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2603.25286v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Negative avoiding sequences of span $n$ are periodic sequences of elements from $\mathbb{Z}_k$ for some $k$ with the property that no $n$-tuple occurs more than once in a period and if an $n$-tuple does occur then its negative does not. They are a special type of cut-down de Bruijn sequence with potential position-location applications. We establish a simple upper bound on the period of such a sequence, and refer to sequences meeting this bound as maximal negative avoiding sequences. We then go on to demonstrate the existence of maximal negative avoiding sequences for every $k\geq3$ and every $n\geq2$.
item.dc:creator: Chris J Mitchell, Peter R Wild

item.title: Magnitude homology of real hyperplane arrangements
item.description: arXiv:2604.03718v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define and study the magnitude and magnitude homology of real hyperplane arrangements by regarding their tope graphs as metric spaces. Since magnitude is a refinement of the cardinality, this may be viewed as a natural generalization of the classical problem of counting the chambers of an arrangement. Our central result is a structure theorem asserting that the magnitude and magnitude homology of an arrangement decompose into contributions indexed by its faces. In particular, the magnitude is determined by the intersection lattice of the arrangement. We also observe several interesting phenomena, including a characterization of Boolean arrangements in terms of diagonality and a reciprocity theorem reminiscent of Ehrhart--Macdonald reciprocity. Finally, based on explicit computations, we conjecture that the magnitude homology of an arrangement is torsion-free and determined by its intersection lattice.
item.dc:creator: Junnosuke Koizumi, Ye Liu

item.title: Cover-free families on graphs
item.description: arXiv:2605.12634v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A family of subsets of a $t$-set is a \emph{$d$-cover-free family} or $d$-CFF if no subset in the family is contained in the union of any $d$ other subsets. Let $t(d, n)$ denote the minimum $t$ for which there exists a $d$-CFF on a $t$-set with $n$ subsets. Since a $1$-CFF is the same as a Sperner family, using Sperner's theorem, we get $t(1, n) \sim \log_{2}(n)$ as $n$ grows. Erd\"os, Frankl, and F\"uredi (JCTA, 1982) proved that $3.106\log_{2}(n) < t(2,n) < 5.512\log_{2}(n)$. This paper focuses on generalizing $1$-CFF and $2$-CFF using a graph $G$ where vertices correspond to subsets in the set system. A $G$-Sperner$(t, n)$ is a family of subsets of a $t$-set such that each edge of $G$ specifies a pair of subsets not contained in each other, where as a $G$-CFF$(t, n)$ is a family of subsets of a $t$-set such that it is $G$-Sperner and the union of a pair of subsets corresponding to each edge of $G$ does not contain any other subset in the family. Let $t_s(G)$ and $t(G)$ denote the minimum $t$ for which there exist a $G$-Sperner$(t, n)$ and a $G$-CFF$(t, n)$, respectively. In this way, $t_s(K_n) = t(1, n)$ and $t(K_n) = t(2, n)$. Firstly, we prove $t_s(G) = t(1, \chi(G))$ for any simple graph $G$ and provide various upper and lower bounds for $t(G)$. The \emph{trivial bound}, $t(1, n) \leq t(G) \leq t(2, n)$ holds for any simple graph $G$ with no isolated vertex, with the lower bound tight for an infinite family of star graphs and the upper bound tight for complete graphs. We study when these bounds can be improved and give better constructive upper bounds for families of graphs such as stars, paths, cycles, wheels, and windmill graphs. In particular, a construction based on mixed-radix Gray codes yields $\log_{2}(n) \leq t(P_n) \leq t(C_n) \leq 1.893\log_{2}(n) + \mathcal{O}(1)$ where $P_n$ and $C_n$ are paths and cycles with $n$ vertices.
item.dc:creator: Prangya Parida, Lucia Moura

item.title: Size and spectral conditions for a graph with given minimum degree to be $k$-$d$-critical
item.description: arXiv:2605.13198v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A $k$-matching in a graph $G$ is defined as a function $f:E(G) \rightarrow \{0,1,\ldots,k\}$ satisfying $\sum_{e\in E_G(v)} f(e)$ $\leq k$ for each vertex $v\in V(G)$, where $E_G(v)$ denotes the set of edges incident to $v$ in $G$. For $1\leq d\leq k$ and $d \equiv |V(G)|~(\mathrm{mod}~2)$, if for any $ v \in V(G)$, there exists a $k$-matching $f$ such that $\sum_{e\in E_G(v)}f(e)=k-d$ and $\sum_{e\in E_G(u)}f(e)=k \text{ for any } u\in V(G)-\{v\}$, then $G$ is $k$-$d$-critical. A graph $G$ of odd order (resp. even order) is generalized factor-critical (resp. generalized bicritical) if the empty set is the unique set attaining the maximum value in $k$-Berge-Tutte-formula of $G$. In this paper, we provide sharp sufficient conditions in terms of size or spectral radius respectively for a graph $G$ to be $k$-$d$-critical, generalized factor-critical and generalized bicritical with minimum degree.
item.dc:creator: Zhenhao Zhang, Xiaogang Liu, Ligong Wang

item.title: Optimal Diameters of High Multiplicity g-Golomb Rulers
item.description: arXiv:2605.14229v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A set $\cG$ of $n$ integers is called a $g$-Golomb ruler if the difference between any two distinct elements of $\cG$ is repeated at most $g$ times. If $g=1$, these are also called $B_2$-sets, Sidon sets, and Babcock sets. We define $G(g,n)$ to be the minimum diameter of a $g$-Golomb ruler with $n$ marks. In this paper, we prove that for every $\epsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large positive integers $b$, if $g\ge(\pi/3+\epsilon)b^{3/2}$, then $G(g,g+b)=g+2b-2$. Explicit thresholds are given for $b\le251$. The main technique is through an arithmetic property of the integers that are \emph{not} in a $g$-Golomb ruler, leading us to introduce LM rulers, a class of rulers where every positive integer distance $d$ occurs as a difference at most $d-1$ times. Writing $L(n)$ for the minimum diameter of an $n$-element LM ruler, we prove $L(n)\ge\sqrt{8/9}\,(n-1)^{3/2}$ for every positive integer $n$ and, using a Farey construction, $L(n)\le(\pi/3+o(1))n^{3/2}$ as $n\to\infty$. We also provide computationally verified optimal LM rulers for every $1\le n\le250$.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Gupta, Kevin O'Bryant

item.title: Spanning triangulations in random graphs
item.description: arXiv:2605.20361v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 1991 Bollob\'{a}s and Frieze found the threshold for the emergence of a spanning triangulation of a triangle in the binomial random graph, up to a logarithmic factor. In this paper, we find the threshold probability for the emergence of a spanning triangulation of a $k$-gon for any $3\leq k\leq n$, up to a constant factor.
item.dc:creator: S. Vakhrushev, M. Zhukovskii

item.title: List coloring uncrowded hypergraphs at the shattering threshold
item.description: arXiv:2606.18048v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A foundational theorem of Ajtai, Koml\'os, Pintz, Spencer, and Szemer\'edi asserts that every $n$-vertex $k$-uniform uncrowded hypergraph (i.e., with girth at least $5$) of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ contains an independent set of size $cn(\log\Delta/\Delta)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$ for some absolute constant $c>0$. Improving an earlier bound of Frieze and Mubayi, Iliopoulos showed that every such hypergraph has list chromatic number at most $(1+o(1))(k-1)(\Delta/\log\Delta)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$. Determining the optimal leading constant in this bound remains a major open problem. A natural target, suggested by the coupon-collector heuristic, is $(k-1)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$, which also corresponds to the shattering threshold for coloring sparse random hypergraphs. Our main result shows that this target is attained: for every integer $k\ge2$, every $k$-uniform uncrowded hypergraph of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ satisfies: $$\chi_\ell(\mathcal{H})\le(1+o(1))\Big((k-1)\frac{\Delta}{\log\Delta}\Big)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}.$$ In particular, this confirms a 2019 conjecture of Molloy for uncrowded hypergraphs. Building on this result, we prove that every $k$-uniform linear hypergraph of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ has chromatic number at most $(c_k+o(1))(\Delta/\log\Delta)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$, where $c_k\to1$ as $k\to\infty$, thereby proving a conjecture of Verstra\"ete and Wilson on the independence number of linear hypergraphs in the stronger form of colorings. Our techniques also yield a palette sparsification theorem for uncrowded hypergraphs, partially answering a question of Casselgren and Eriksson.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Dhawan, Abhishek Methuku, Minh-Quan Vo

item.title: The unique self-dual binary code of length 26 with minimum weight 6
item.description: arXiv:2606.24573v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The binary Type I self-dual [26,13,6] code is classical. We give what appears to be the first direct non-computational proof of its uniqueness. We first determine the weight enumerators of the code and its shadow. Degree-one harmonic MacWilliams identities supply the required 1-designs. Elementary intersection counts then show that the two minimal half-shadows each contain 13 words; these words label the 26 coordinates as 13 points and 13 lines, and the two shadow classes become the point-stars and line-stars. From this structure we give two uniqueness proofs: one reconstructs the projective plane of order 3 and the plane code, including the full automorphism group PGL(3,3):2; the other deletes an intrinsic flag, obtains the odd Golay code together with a deep hole coset, and reconstructs the length 26 code and the size of the automorphism group from this coset datum. Thus the natural length-24 object behind the code is the odd Golay code together with its unique orbit of deep hole cosets.
item.dc:creator: Gerald H\"ohn

item.title: An annihilation-number Caro-Wei bound: a TxGraffiti conjecture and an independence-number bracket
item.description: arXiv:2606.29553v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The independence number $\alpha$ of a finite simple graph lies between the polynomial-time computable Havel-Hakimi residue $R$ and annihilation number $a$. The Caro-Wei sum $W$ gives another lower bound and the known upper bound $\alpha\le(\Delta+1)W/2$ for maximum degree $\Delta\ge1$. This upper bound does not by itself control the larger quantity $a$. This note proves $a\le(\Delta+1)W/2$ for $\Delta\ge1$, with equality attained, for example, by regular graphs of positive degree and even order. Together with $R\ge W$, this bound shows that the interval from $R$ to $a$ improves or matches both Caro-Wei endpoints. Its sharp worst-case endpoint ratio remains $(\Delta+1)/2$, even among connected graphs. For maximum degree at least three, the bound also proves the inequality $\alpha\ge(a+R)/\Delta$ conjectured by TxGraffiti, an automated conjecturing program. A direct calculation handles connected graphs of maximum degree two. Together these cases resolve the conjecture for every connected graph with at least three vertices. The single edge is the only nontrivial connected exception. Equality holds for exactly eight connected graphs up to isomorphism. For maximum degree at least three, the conjectured lower bound never exceeds the residue, so it gives no stronger independence estimate.
item.dc:creator: Chakshu Gupta

item.title: AVD Total Colorings of Subdivision Graphs, Joins, and Deleted Lexicographic Products
item.description: arXiv:2607.01979v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 2020, Panda, Verma, and Keerti asked whether the central graph of every graph satisfies the AVD-total coloring conjecture (AVD-TCC). In this paper, we use idempotent commutative Latin squares and a theorem of Borodin, Kostochka, and Woodall to prove the AVD-TCC for central graphs of all connected graphs with order at least five and minimum degree at least two. We further determine the AVD-total chromatic number of subdivision graphs of connected graphs and establish new results on the AVD-total coloring of joins of graphs, central graphs, and deleted lexicographic products.
item.dc:creator: Amitayu Banerjee

item.title: On the Harborth Conjecture. Part I. Quadrilaterals
item.description: arXiv:2607.02535v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Harborth conjecture states that every planar graph has a crossing-free straight-line drawing in which every edge has an integer length. Kleber's strengthening asks for the vertices themselves to have integer coordinates. In this series of papers, we make progress towards settling these conjectures. Kleber's conjecture reduces to local rational-distance statements for special polygons with at most five vertices. The triangle case is known from the results of Almering and Berry. In this paper, we prove the existence of a rational-distance point on an interior integer diagonal in all the cases for non-degenerate and degenerate quadrilaterals. In the upcoming papers, we focus on non-degenerate and degenerate pentagons.
item.dc:creator: Shiva Kintali

item.title: A polynomial criterion for DP-coloring of uncrowded hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2607.05256v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a color-degree criterion for DP-coloring of finite uncrowded hypergraphs of bounded rank. For a $q$-fold cover with edge sizes between $2$ and $r+1$, let $D_\ell$ be the maximum number of forbidden colorings on $(\ell+1)$-edges prescribing a fixed color at a fixed vertex. If $q$ is sufficiently large in terms of $r$, then the cover admits a coloring whenever \[ \sum_{\ell=1}^r\frac{D_\ell}{q^\ell}\leq\log q-20\log\log q. \] For uncrowded $(r+1)$-uniform hypergraphs of maximum degree $\Delta$, this gives a DP-chromatic number at most $(1+O_r(\log\log\Delta/\log\Delta))(r\Delta/\log\Delta)^{1/r}$.
item.dc:creator: Jing Yu, Junchi Zhang

item.title: Triple arrays from ovals in finite projective planes
item.description: arXiv:2607.20275v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we prove that whenever a projective plane of odd order n contains an oval, it may be used to construct a triple array with n + 1 rows, n.n columns and n(n + 1) symbols. In particular, for any odd prime power s, we use the projective plane over the field of order s to construct an explicitly given (s + 1) times s.s triple array on s(s + 1) symbols. This is only the third infinite series of triple arrays (up to transposition) to be found. Our construction proves a recent conjecture of Gordeev and Ohman (2025) in the case of odd prime powers.
item.dc:creator: Sunanda Bagchi, Bhaskar Bagchi

item.title: The maximum domination number of $k$-majority tournaments
item.description: arXiv:2607.23148v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A tournament is a \emph{$k$-majority tournament} if it is the pairwise majority relation of an election with $2k-1$ voters: there are $2k-1$ linear orders of the vertex set, repetitions allowed, such that $u\to v$ exactly when $u$ precedes $v$ in at least $k$ of them. Let $F(k)$ be the maximum domination number of a $k$-majority tournament. In 2006, Alon, Brightwell, Kierstead, Kostochka and Winkler proved that $F(k)$ is finite and that $c_1k/\log k\le F(k)\le c_2k\log k$ for absolute constants $c_1,c_2>0$; the order of growth of $F(k)$ has been open since. We prove that $F(k)=\Theta(k\log k)$. As a consequence, the maximum domination number of a tournament realized by fair $m$-sided dice is $\Theta(m\log m)$, closing the corresponding gap in the bounds of Alon et al.
item.dc:creator: Jiangdong Ai, Xiangjie Yi

item.title: On the Thickness of Infinite Generalized Sidon Sets, II
item.dc:creator: Kevin O'Bryant

item.title: New upper bound for multicolor Ramsey numbers
item.description: arXiv:2608.01962v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $R_r(k)$ denote the diagonal $r$-color graph Ramsey number. We prove that there exist absolute constants $c,K>0$ such that \[ R_r(k)\le \exp\!\left(-c\frac{k}{r^2\log^4(2r)}\right)r^{rk} \] for every $r\ge2$ and every $k\ge Kr^2\log^6(2r)$. The proof combines a positive-coefficient root filter of variable order with a retained-spine refinement of the multicolor book method.b
item.dc:creator: Gang Yang, Yaping Mao

item.title: Asymptotic Bounds for Online Ramsey Numbers of Stars versus Long Paths and Cycles
item.description: arXiv:2608.27405v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The online Ramsey game for graphs $G$ and $H$ is played on the infinite complete graph $K_\mathbb{N}$. In each round, Builder chooses an edge, and Painter colors it red or blue. The online Ramsey number $\tilde{r}(G,H)$ is the smallest integer $t$ for which Builder has a strategy guaranteeing a red copy of $G$ or a blue copy of $H$ within $t$ rounds. For every fixed integer $k\ge4$, the best-known asymptotic lower bounds for $\tilde{r}(K_{1,k},P_n)$ and $\tilde{r}(K_{1,k},C_n)$ are $\left(\frac{k+3}{4}+o(1)\right)n$ as $n\to\infty$. We improve the corresponding asymptotic upper bounds from $\left(k+o(1)\right)n$ to $\left(\frac{k+3}{3}+o(1)\right)n$ as $n\to\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Sam Beilis, Israel R. Curbelo, Elizabeth R. Koizumi

item.title: A note on the diameter of graphs of two-dimensional simplex codes
item.description: arXiv:2609.13574v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Gs(2,q)$ denote the graph induced in the Grassmann graph by the $q$-ary simplex codes of dimension $2$. We determine its diameter for every prime power $q$. The cases $q=2,3$ are elementary, while the diameter for $q=4$ follows from a known description of the distance relation. We prove that the diameter equals $3$ for every $q\ge5$, so that it is $0$ for $q=2$, $2$ for $q=3$, and $3$ for all $q\ge4$. The proof uses the realization of two-dimensional simplex codes as projective lines and a ratio criterion for collinearity of simplex points. A consequence of a theorem of Marshall Hall on finite abelian groups yields a bridge lemma and gives the uniform upper bound $3$. To obtain the matching lower bound for $q\ge5$, we construct an explicit diagonal pair of simplex lines and rule out a common neighbor by two independent arguments, one based on moments and the other on products. For $q\ge7$, we also give an independent counting proof. The case $q=4$ is treated separately. In particular, for $q\ge4$ the simplex-code graph is not isometrically embedded in the ambient Grassmann graph.
item.dc:creator: Artur Siemaszko

item.title: An involution on Dyck paths in the region $\defc\le\min(\area,\dinv)$ that interchanges area and dinv
item.description: arXiv:2609.21403v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct an explicit involution on Dyck paths satisfying $\defc\le\min(\area,\dinv)$ that interchanges area and dinv, where $\defc=\binom n2-\area-\dinv$ and $n$ is the semilength. In addition, we give an involution on Dyck paths with $\defc \le 2n-8$ that interchanges area and dinv. Finally, we give an explicit partition formula for the portion of the $q,t$-Catalan polynomial of total degree at least $\binom n2-2n+8$, thereby proving a conjecture of Lee and Li~\cite[Conjecture~4]{LeeLi11}. Altogether our results give a combinatorial explanation of $q,t$-Catalan symmetry in the region $\defc\le\max(2n-8,\min(\area,\dinv))$. Our constructions rely on a number of new combinatorial objects developed here and three main external tools: the dual Dyck insertion of \cite{Hawkes26}, the Garsia--Milne involution principle~\cite{GarsiaMilne81,Doyle19}, and the partition bijection of ~\cite{LoehrWarrington09}. We also explore rational analogs of these results, give an answer to Question~4.9 of Kiem and Lee~\cite{KiemLee24} and consider deficit up to $3n-15$ briefly.
item.dc:creator: Graham Hawkes

item.title: A Log-Star Comparison Between Expectation Threshold and Fractional Expectation Threshold
item.description: arXiv:2609.30680v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We proved a log-star comparison between the expectation threshold $q(\mathcal F)$ and the fractional expectation threshold $q_f(\mathcal F)$ for any nontrivial increasing family $\mathcal F$ on a finite ground set $V$ of size $|V|=N$. Specifically, we show that $$q_f(\mathcal F)\le64\log_2^*(N+2)\,q(\mathcal F),$$ where $\log_2^* x$ is the iterated logarithm of base-2. Using similiar methods, one can extend this result to the following stronger form: there exists a universal constant $C>0$ such that \[ q_f(\mathcal F)\le Cq(\mathcal F)\log_2^*(l(\mathcal F)),\quad q_f(\mathcal F)\le Cq(\mathcal F)\log_2^*(\operatorname{VC}(\min\mathcal F)), \] where $l(\mathcal F):=\max\{2,\max_{S\in\min\mathcal F}|S|\}$ and $\operatorname{VC}(\min\mathcal F)$ denotes the VC-dimension of $\min\mathcal F$. On October 7, 2026, OpenAI released a result proving the equivalence of fractional and integral thresholds, which supersedes the findings in this note. The authors are keeping this note for historical reference.
item.dc:creator: Xuan Fang, Tianyu Wang

item.title: Nonlinear lower-tail large deviations at criticality
item.description: arXiv:2610.10233v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce general methods to derive lower tail large deviation principles, for a variety of nonlinear problems of combinatorial interest. These methods are especially effective in "critical" regimes, where the nonlinearities are not sparse enough for Poissonian lower tails (e.g., Janson's inequality does not provide a sharp tail bound), but the situation is not so dense that combinatorial effects dominate (e.g., we cannot directly apply the theory of hypergraph containers or the relative entropy framework of Kozma-Samotij). In particular, these are regimes where one expects interesting phase transitions to occur. Our results have a number of consequences related to subgraphs in random graphs, answering various questions of Warnke and Jenssen-Perkins-Potukuchi-Simkin. For example, consider a random graph $G\sim \mathbb G(n,p)$, and let $L_\triangle(n,p)=\log\Pr[G\text{ is triangle-free}]$. The first-order asymptotics of $L_\triangle(n,p)$ have long been known in all parameter ranges except the critical regime where $p$ has order of magnitude $1/\sqrt n$. We are able to fill this gap: for any fixed $c>0$, we show that $n^{-3/2}L_\triangle(n,c/\sqrt n)$ converges to a limit expressed in terms of a two-parameter variational problem, which has a single phase transition at $c\approx 4.341$. In contrast, we show that there is no such phase transition for the probability that $G$ is $C_{2\ell}$-free, for any fixed even cycle $C_{2\ell}$. We also obtain some applications in combinatorial design theory. Addressing conjectures of Glock-K\"uhn-Lo-Osthus, Kelly, and Kwan-Sah-Sawhney-Simkin, we obtain new estimates on the number of order-$n$ Steiner triple systems with no Pasch configuration and the number of order-$n$ Latin squares with no $2\times 2$ Latin subsquare (both tight up to a factor of $\exp(o(n^2))$).
item.dc:creator: Matthew Kwan, Huy Tuan Pham

item.title: Symmetric, rational and infinitely many $(23_4)$ configurations, and the end of the existence problem for geometric $(n_4)$ configurations
item.description: arXiv:2610.14099v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A geometric $(n_4)$ configuration is a set of $n$ points and $n$ lines in the real projective plane such that every point lies on exactly four of the lines and every line contains exactly four of the points. The question of which $n$ admit such a configuration was posed by Gr\"unbaum in 2000, and successive work of Bokowski, Gr\"unbaum, Schewe, Pilaud and Cuntz settled every case but $n=23$. We settle this last case by bounding the symmetry of such configurations and classifying the most symmetric ones exactly. We prove that for every prime $n\equiv3\pmod4$ the group of projective symmetries of a geometric $(n_4)$ configuration has order at most four, explaining why symmetric constructions failed at $n=23$, and the same argument bounds the symmetry of $(n_5)$ configurations for primes $n\not\equiv1\pmod5$. Reducing the Klein four-group case to 4021 bilinear polynomial systems and solving all of them exactly with Gr\"obner bases, we show that exactly two $(23_4)$ configurations reach this bound up to projective equivalence and that there are no others even over $\mathbb{C}$. Both are self-polar; the first has integer coordinates and the second is defined over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{17})$ but not over $\mathbb{Q}$. Consequently geometric $(n_4)$ configurations exist if and only if $n\ge18$ and $n\ne19$. The same classification recovers Cuntz's $(22_4)$ and $(26_4)$ configurations and finds three new combinatorial types at $n=22$ and $94$ at $n=26$. Among self-polar $(23_4)$ configurations with a single involution we find $50$ more, defined over number fields of degree at most $7$. Four of them deform in one-parameter families, and computing three of these exactly, one birational to the modular curve $X_1(11)$, we prove that there are infinitely many geometric $(23_4)$ configurations, among them infinitely many with rational coordinates that are self-polar and have no projective symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Wenhao Lu

item.title: On the Stability of the Independence Number of the Distance Graph G(n,r,<s) for Growing r and s
item.description: arXiv:2610.16955v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a random subgraph G_p(n,r,<s) of the complete distance graph G(n,r,<s) whose vertices are the r-element subsets of the set {1,...,n} and whose edges join pairs of subsets that intersect in fewer than s elements; each edge survives independently of the others with probability p. The stability of the Erdos-Ko-Rado theorem is the event that the independence number of the random subgraph equals that of the original graph, N = C_{n-s}^{r-s}. For fixed r and s, two-sided bounds for the critical probability, whose ratio depends on r and s, were obtained by P. A. Ogarok and A. M. Raigorodskii. In this paper we establish the order of the critical probability for growing r=r(n) and s=s(n): if min{C_r^s r^2, s r^3} = o(n), then the upper and lower bounds differ only by an absolute constant factor. The proof is elementary; only one of the two branches of the growth condition uses the complete nontrivial-intersection theorem of Ahlswede-Khachatrian.
item.dc:creator: Vsevolod A. Pokhachevskiy, Andrei Raigorodskii

item.title: Sensitivity of Rotation Symmetric Boolean Functions via Binary Necklaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.17006v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Rotation symmetric Boolean functions are important structured families in the theory of Boolean functions, where cyclic invariance permits compact algebraic descriptions while retaining nontrivial local behavior. We investigate their sensitivity through binary necklaces and monomial orbit sums. In the necklace quotient of the Boolean cube, ordinary adjacency does not record the number of coordinate flips: we give a directed flip-multiplicity formula involving stabilizers and distance-two near-periods, and derive exact local sensitivity formulas when the number of variables is an odd prime. For monomial rotation symmetric functions we determine sensitivity for all odd degrees and for quadratic orbit sums. For the consecutive-monomial family of every even degree $d\ge4$, we prove a run-cluster inequality and obtain the eventual exact formula $s(F_{d,n})=n-\min\{r,d+2-r\}$, where $n\equiv r\pmod{d+2}$, under the stated length hypothesis. The consecutive quartic case follows explicitly. We also evaluate sensitivity for cyclic run-threshold functions. Our results provide exact combinatorial and complexity-theoretic information about cyclic Boolean functions and clarify how cyclic symmetry governs local sensitivity.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Li, Jing Zhang

item.title: Block Sensitivity and Certificate Complexity of Rotation Symmetric Boolean Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.17100v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate block sensitivity and certificate complexity of monomial rotation-symmetric Boolean functions, obtaining exact formulas and structural classifications for several families. For odd-degree monomial rotation-symmetric functions, the equality $s(f)=n$ established in our earlier work yields $bs(f)=C(f)=n$. For quadratic monomial rotation-symmetric functions, we determine both measures completely and prove that block sensitivity equals certificate complexity.
