For consecutive quartic monomials, we determine sensitivity, block sensitivity, and certificate complexity in every residue class of the number of variables. Our principal result is an exact global block-sensitivity formula for consecutive monomials of every even degree $d\ge4$. Writing $n=q(d+2)+\rho$, where $0\le\rho<d+2$ and $q\ge\max\{2,d/2-1\}$, we prove \[ bs(F_{d,n})=n-\min\left\{\left\lceil\frac{\rho}{2}\right\rceil,d+2-\rho\right\}. \] We also establish the corresponding sensitivity formula by a self-contained argument, yielding arbitrarily large gaps between sensitivity and block sensitivity as the degree varies. For certificate complexity, we obtain exact pointwise formulas for structured run-and-gap configurations and establish additional global equalities, including $C(F_{6,8q+5})=bs(F_{6,8q+5})=8q+2$ for $q\ge2$. Our methods combine cyclic run decomposition, parity arguments, explicit sensitive-block constructions, and constant-subcube certificates. The exact global certificate complexity for arbitrary even degrees remains open.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Li, Jing Zhang

item.title: Positivity and negativity for $h$-bases for $n$
item.description: arXiv:2610.19470v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A set $A$ of integers is an $h$-basis for $n$ if every integer in $[0,n] = \{0,1,2,\ldots,n\}$ belongs to the sumset $hA$, that is, can be represented as the sum of exactly $h$ not necessarily distinct elements of $A$. The classical postage stamp problem asks for the largest integer $n_h(k)$ such that $[0,n_h(k)] \subseteq hA$ for some set $A$ of nonnegative integers of size $k+1$. We consider the effect of allowing negative elements. Let $n^{\flat}_h(k)$ be the largest integer such that $[0,n^{\flat}_h(k)] \subseteq hA$ for some set $A$ of integers of size $k+1$ containing at least one negative integer. For $k=2$, we have $n^{\flat}_h(2) < n_h(2)$ if $h$ is odd or $h=4$ and $n^{\flat}_h(2) = n_h(2)$ if $h$ is even and $h \neq 4$. Proofs of these comparison results were autonomously discovered and formally verified in Lean by https://aristotle.harmonic.fun/}{Aristotle}, a formal reasoning agent developed by https://www.harmonic.fun/}{Harmonic}. In this paper we give new proofs of these results.
item.dc:creator: Wouter van Doorn, Pietro Monticone, Melvyn B. Nathanson

item.title: Ehrhart positivity for paving positroids
item.description: arXiv:2610.21501v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A central conjecture of Ferroni, Jochemko, and Schr\"{o}ter posits that every positroid is Ehrhart positive. While Ehrhart positivity has recently been verified for notable classes such as lattice path matroids and series-parallel matroids, the general conjecture remains open. In this paper, we prove that the base polytope of any paving positroid has positive Ehrhart coefficients. This establishes a new class of Ehrhart positive positroids and provides substantial evidence supporting this conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Feihu Liu, Zihao Zhang

item.title: Orlik-Solomon algebras determine the Tutte polynomials of matroids of rank at most three
item.description: arXiv:2610.21812v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a simple matroid of rank $r$ on the ground set $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $T_{\mathcal{M}}(x,y)$ denote its Tutte polynomial, and let $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{M})$ denote its Orlik-Solomon $\mathbb{C}$-algebra. We say that $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{M})$ determines $T_{\mathcal{M}}(x,y)$ if, for every simple matroid $\mathcal{N}$, an isomorphism $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{M})\cong\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{N})$ of $\mathbb{C}$-algebras, without regard to the grading, implies $T_{\mathcal{M}}(x,y)=T_{\mathcal{N}}(x,y)$. Falk conjectured that the Orlik-Solomon $\mathbb{C}$-algebra of every simple matroid of rank three determines its Tutte polynomial. We prove that this holds for every simple matroid of rank at most three, thereby resolving Falk's conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Jianxuan Luo, Tingzeng Wu, Hong-Jian Lai

item.title: Exact Realization of Edge and Induced Three-Vertex Subgraph Counts
item.description: arXiv:2610.30166v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The study of three-vertex subgraph densities has developed along two complementary lines: exact finite realization in large graphs of a given order, and asymptotic approximate realization by sequences of graphs. We bridge these viewpoints for the edge density and the four induced three-vertex subgraph densities. By analyzing local modifications of finite samples from graphons, we show that, for any nonempty subset of these densities, every asymptotically feasible target vector lying a fixed positive distance from the boundary of the corresponding feasible region is realized exactly by a graph of every sufficiently large order, subject only to the natural arithmetic constraints. Thus, in the interior of these feasible regions, asymptotic feasibility implies exact finite realizability up to the unavoidable arithmetic obstructions.
item.dc:creator: Hillel Schein

item.title: Prime Nullspace Matrices and Even Dominating Sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.31475v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A non-zero $m \times n$ (0, 1)-matrix $A$ is called a {\em nullspace matrix} if each entry $(i, j)$ of $A$ has an even number of $1's$ in the set of entries consisting of $(i, j)$ and its rectilinear neighbors. These matrices correspond to even dominating sets of $m \times n$ grid graphs. We study these matrices and consider those that cannot be constructed from smaller nullspace matrices.
item.dc:creator: William F. Klostermeyer

item.title: Swapping Compatible Words
item.description: arXiv:2610.31967v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 1981 Guibas and Odlyzko showed that the set $A$ of all words of a given length $n$ that avoid a given word $p$, and the set $B$ of all words of length $n$ that avoid a given word $q$, have the same cardinality if and only if $p$ and $q$ have the same self-border lengths. Carrigan et.~ al.~ ask in if there is a ``natural'' bijection between $A$ and $B$. This paper makes partial progress toward answering that question. We provide such a bijection by imposing additional conditions on $p$ and $q$, but we also obtain a stronger conclusion: there is a ``natural'' bijection $\Phi$ from the set of all finite words to itself that swaps $p$ and $q$ in each word $\Omega$, meaning that $\Omega$ has a $p$ or $q$ at a given position iff $\Phi(\Omega)$ has, repectively, a $q$ or a $p$ at that same position. An algorithm is given for converting $\Omega$ into $\Phi(\Omega)$.
item.dc:creator: Ramin Naimi

item.title: Minimum orders of clique oddomorphism counterexamples
item.description: arXiv:2610.33283v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An oddomorphism to $K_n$ is a proper colouring with $n$ colours in which every vertex is designated odd or even, every vertex has in each other colour class a number of neighbours of its own parity, and every colour class contains an odd number of odd vertices. We prove that an oddomorphism witness to $K_n$ on at most $n+6$ vertices contains a $K_n$ minor with every branch meeting the witness's specified odd set. The conclusion holds inside any graph containing the witness and therefore applies to weak oddomorphisms. The bound is sharp: for every $n\ge8$ the minimum order of a graph admitting a weak oddomorphism to $K_n$ but having no $K_n$ minor is exactly $n+7$. The extremal example is a fifteen-vertex graph with an oddomorphism to $K_8$, obtained from the doubled theta graph of Kriesell and Mohr by adding one vertex adjacent to the seven roots; we give a structural proof that it has no $K_8$ minor, including their counting argument for the rooted case. We also prove that every witness to $K_4$, of arbitrary order, has a $K_4$ minor with every branch meeting its original odd set. The roots need not be prescribed or have distinct colours. In six colours, we prove that a fibre of size at most two forces a $K_5$ minor rooted in the original odd set, with no bound on the other fibres. In particular every six-colour witness on at most seventeen vertices has such a model. A separate technical companion records further results on related root-apex graphs, an attachment theorem and a bounded nine-colour statement, together with their computational provenance; none of it is used here. The qualitative clique-target existence problem has been solved in recent work; our results concern exact source-order bounds and control of the original odd set.
item.dc:creator: Michal \v{C}ert\'ik

item.title: Sharp enumeration and growth of admissible sets of integers
item.description: arXiv:2610.34372v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A set of positive integers is admissible if equal sums of finite subsets always have equal numbers of summands. Let $a(N)$ count the nonempty admissible subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$, and let $b(N)$ count those with maximum $N$. We prove $\log a(N)\sim\log b(N)\sim\pi\sqrt{2N/3}$, establishing the sharp logarithmic asymptotic proposed by Nicolas. More generally, let $Q_h(N)$ count the subsets for which each integer has subset-sum representations of at most $h$ distinct cardinalities. Uniformly for all positive integers $h,N$, we prove $\log Q_h(N)\asymp\min\{N,\sqrt{hN}\}$ with absolute implied constants. Every infinite set satisfying the same condition for some fixed $h$ has counting function $o(\sqrt x)$. At $h=1$, the latter two results settle conjectures of Erd\H{o}s, Nicolas and S\'ark\"ozy, strengthening the proposed vanishing lower limit to a full limit. The proofs record each subset sum together with its cardinality and use the counting theorem of Campos and the structure theorem of Carpenter, Defant and Kravitz. The sharp count also uses Nicolas's partition enumeration and an elementary construction of a long restricted-sum progression. Finally, we give an exact partition formula for the odd sets with separated alternate cardinality layers suggested by Nicolas.
item.dc:creator: Guoqing Wang, Wenkai Yang

item.title: Diameter Bounds and Finiteness of Graphs from Local Intersection Data
item.description: arXiv:2610.36620v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend the Bakry--\'Emery curvature framework on graphs, broadening its applications and strengthening the resulting diameter bounds. We study diameter bounds and finiteness for amply regular graphs, distance-regular graphs, $(s,c,a,k)$-graphs, and locally strongly regular graphs. In particular, for an amply regular graph with parameters $(v,k,\lambda,\mu)$, we prove that \[{\rm{diam}}(G)\le4+8\log\frac{k}{\max\{\lambda,\mu\}}\] when $\mu>2$ and $k\ge3\lambda^2/\mu$, improving the previous linear bound $4k/(\lambda+4)$ to a logarithmic bound. We also address several related conjectures. In their monograph \emph{Distance-Regular Graphs}, Brouwer, Cohen, and Neumaier conjectured that every amply regular graph with $\mu>1$, except the icosahedron, satisfies ${\rm{diam}}(G)\le2k/(\lambda+2)$. We confirm this bound when $\mu>\lambda+1$ and give counterexamples to the conjecture with $\mu=\lambda$. For amply regular graphs with $\mu\ge\lambda$ and $\mu>1$, we obtain ${\rm{diam}}(G)\le 2k/\mu+1$. This proves the Qiao--Park--Koolen conjecture. In 1983, Terwilliger conjectured that every $(s,c,a,k)$-graph with $c>1$ is finite. We prove this conjecture when ``$s>2$, $c>2$, $(s,c)\ne(4,3)$'' and when ``$s=2$, $c>7$''. Moreover, we prove Weetman's finiteness conjecture for locally strongly regular graphs when the local parameter $\mu>1$, and disprove his stronger conjecture that every strongly regular graph is an $\mathscr{S}$-graph. We also prove that every graph whose local graphs all have rank 3 is finite, which in particular proves a conjecture of Soicher in 1992.
item.dc:creator: Kaizhe Chen

item.title: Proper conflict-free degree-choosability of graphs with maximum average degree less than $8/3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.41668v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A proper coloring $\varphi$ of a graph $G$ is called proper conflict-free if, for every non-isolated vertex $v$, some color appears exactly once in its open neighborhood $N_G(v)$. For a nonnegative integer $k$, a graph $G$ is proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+k)$-choosable if, for every list assignment $L$ satisfying $|L(v)|\ge d_G(v)+k$ for each $v\in V(G)$, there exists a proper conflict-free coloring $\varphi$ of $G$ with $\varphi(v)\in L(v)$ for each $v\in V(G)$. We prove that every connected graph other than the $5$-cycle $C_5$ with maximum average degree less than $8/3$ is proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+2)$-choosable. This improves the maximum average degree bound $18/7$ of Kashima, \v{S}krekovski and Xu, and removes the assumption $g(G)\ge7$ from the $8/3$ theorem of Qi, Song and Cao. We also show that the $(\mathrm{degree}+2)$ list-size bound is best possible for graphs with maximum average degree arbitrarily close to $8/3$ from below. As an immediate consequence, our theorem implies that every planar graph of girth at least $8$ is proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+2)$-choosable.
item.dc:creator: Huijuan Xu

item.title: A $33$-polynomial proof of a three-color Rado number formula
item.description: arXiv:2611.01714v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $k\ge 3$, let $T_k(3)$ denote the least $N$ such that every $3$-coloring of $[1,N]$ contains a monochromatic solution to $x+(k-1)y=z$. The formula $T_k(3)=k^3+2k^2-2$ is already known: it follows from a Theorem of Chang, De Loera, and Wesley. Their proof uses a symbolic SAT certificate with $685$ polynomials and $9468$ solution triples. The purpose of this paper is to give an independent, explicit proof based on a much smaller certificate. We exhibit a fixed set $\Xmin$ of $33$ polynomials in $k$ and the $144$ polynomial identities $z=x+(k-1)y$ among them, and show that no $3$-coloring of $\Xmin$ avoids a monochromatic identity. The resulting case analysis has $62$ cases, depth $8$, and uses only two elementary rules; it is given in full and independently checked by a program. We also prove that $\Xmin$ is a critical subset of minimum cardinality of the $51$-element set from which it was extracted, and describe the rigid structure shared by all extremal colorings of $[1,k^3+2k^2-3]$. The lower bound is supplied by an explicit recursive coloring. In the notation $s_a(3)$ of the first author, with $a=k-1$, the formula is $s_a(3)=a^3+5a^2+7a+1$, which was conjectured before.
item.dc:creator: Amir Khamseh, Mohammad Hassan Safareh

item.title: Counterexamples to Relaxed Multiplication in List Coloring
item.description: arXiv:2611.03151v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Jiang and Zhu [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 137 (2019) 112--117] asked whether every $k$-choosable graph is $(km+1:m)$-choosable for every positive integer $m$. We show that, for all integers $k\ge3$, $m\ge2$, and $t\ge0$ satisfying $m>8t+\epsilon$, where $\epsilon\in\{0,1\}$ and $m\equiv\epsilon\pmod2$, there is a graph with chromatic number and choice number both equal to $k$ that is not $(km+t:m)$-choosable. This answers their question negatively for every $k\ge3$ and $m\ge10$. In particular, our construction yields a $3$-choosable graph on $91$ vertices that is not $(6:2)$-choosable, answering a question of Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Hu and Sereni [Adv. Comb. (2019), Paper No.~5]. More generally, for every fixed $b\ge1$, $m\ge2$, and $t\ge0$, we construct an $(a:b)$-choosable graph that is not $(am+t:bm)$-choosable for all sufficiently large $a$, with an explicit bound on $a$. Let $F(a,b)$ be the supremum of the strong fractional choice numbers of $(a:b)$-choosable graphs. We prove that for every fixed $b\ge1$, $F(a,b)-\frac ab$ tends to infinity as $a\to\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Xiaolan Hu, Jiao Li

item.title: Automaticity of structural defects in fixed points of block substitutions
item.description: arXiv:2611.04880v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study structural defects in fixed points of block substitutions, building on arXiv:2604.12637 and providing its technical supplement. We develop an automata-based framework to characterize their occurrence and derive verifiable combinatorial criteria. We also introduce simplifications for the construction and analysis of these automata, including tensor-product decompositions, that clarify the mechanisms underlying structural defects and their emergence.
item.dc:creator: Lior Tenenbaum

item.title: A near-quadratic lower bound for the Brown--Erd\H{o}s--S\'os $(9,6)$-problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.05261v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For integers $e\ge3$, let $f_3(n,e+3,e)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $3$-uniform hypergraph containing no $e$ distinct edges spanning at most $e+3$ vertices. The lower-bound part of a longstanding conjecture of Erd\H{o}s, Frankl, and R\"odl from 1986 asserts that $f_3(n,e+3,e)\ge n^{2-o(1)}$ for every fixed $e\ge3$. We prove that $f_3(n,9,6)\ge n^2\exp(-O((\log n)^{2/3}))$, resolving the first open case not covered by the classical construction of Ruzsa and Szemer\'edi in 1976, which established $f_3(n,6,3)\ge n^{2-o(1)}$. We also establish near-quadratic lower bounds for $f_3(n,e+3,e)$ with $e=9,10,11$. We further extend the result for $e=6$ to every fixed uniformity $r\ge4$.
item.dc:creator: Xiangliang Kong, Chong Shangguan, Xin Wang

item.title: A family of symmetric counterexamples to the bent sum decomposition conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.06744v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we provide an infinite family of counterexamples to Tokareva's conjecture on sums of two bent functions. The conjecture states that every Boolean function in an even number of variables $n$ of algebraic degree at most $n/2$ can be written as the sum of two bent functions. We show that for every $n=2^k\geq 8$, the symmetric function $F_n=1+\sigma_2+\sigma_4+\sigma_6+\cdots+\sigma_{n/2}$ has degree $n/2$ and cannot be written as a sum of at most two bent functions. Here $\sigma_j$ is the elementary symmetric Boolean polynomial of degree $j$. Furthermore, we show that the eight-variable member of this family can be represented as the sum of exactly three bent functions. Using the connection between bent-sum decompositions and derivatives of bent functions, we also obtain an infinite family of balanced Boolean functions that cannot be derivatives of bent functions.
item.dc:creator: M\'at\'e R\'obert Kepes, Anita Kercs\'o-Moln\'ar, Andr\'as Viczi\'an

item.title: Gaps in the Most Frequent Sizes of Integer Sumsets
item.description: arXiv:2611.07303v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Nathanson observed that, for four-element sets $A$ of integers, the most frequent sizes of the iterated sumset $hA$ are separated by triangular numbers. Senger proved this and suggested an analogue for larger sets. We establish this pattern for $k$-element subsets of $\{1,\ldots,q\}$, for every fixed $k\geq3$, where $h\geq2$ is either fixed or grows slower than $q^{1/(2k-1)}$. As $q\to\infty$, almost every such set has the largest possible $h$-fold sumset, and almost every exception has one of $h-1$ explicit smaller sizes. The differences between consecutive sizes among these $h$ values are consecutive $(k-2)$-dimensional simplex numbers.
item.dc:creator: Saad A. Awan, Steven J. Miller, Linh Nguyen, Steven Senger, Elvis Wong

item.title: Trees in Random Sparse Graphs with a Given Degree Sequence
item.description: arXiv:1401.0220v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathbb{G}^{D}$ be the set of graphs $G(V,\, E)$ with $\left|V\right|=n$, and the degree sequence equal to $D=(d_{1},\, d_{2},\,\dots,\, d_{n})$. In addition, for $\frac{1}{2}<a<1$, we define the set of graphs with an almost given degree sequence $D$ as follows, \[ \mathbb{G}_{a}^{D}:=\cup\,\mathbb{G}^{\bar{D}}, \] where the union is over all degree sequences $\bar{D}$ such that, for $1\leq i\leq n$, we have $\left|d_{i}-\bar{d}_{i}\right|<d_{i}^{a}$. Now, if we chose random graphs $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{g}}\left(D\right)$ and $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{a}}\left(D\right)$ uniformly out of the sets $\mathbb{G}^{D}$ and $\mathbb{G}_{a}^{D}$, respectively, what do they look like? This has been studied when $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{g}}\left(D\right)$ is a dense graph, i.e. $\left|E\right|=\Theta(n^{2})$, in the sense of graphons, or when $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{g}}\left(D\right)$ is very sparse, i.e. $d_{n}^{2}=o(\left|E\right|)$. In the case of sparse graphs with an almost given degree sequence, we investigate this question, and give the finite tree subgraph structure of $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{a}}\left(D\right)$ under some mild conditions. For the random graph $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{g}}\left(D\right)$ with a given degree sequence, we re-derive the finite tree structure in dense and very sparse cases to give a continuous picture. Moreover, for a pair of vectors $\left(D_{1},D_{2}\right)\in\mathbb{Z}^{n_{1}}\times\mathbb{Z}^{n_{2}}$, we let $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{b}}\left(D_{1},D_{2}\right)$ be the random bipartite graph that is chosen uniformly out of the set $\mathbb{G}^{D_{1},D_{2}}$, where $\mathbb{G}^{D_{1},D_{2}}$ is the set of all bipartite graphs with the degree sequence $\left(D_{1},D_{2}\right)$. We are able to show the result for $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{b}}\left(D_{1},D_{2}\right)$ without any further conditions.
item.dc:creator: Behzad Mehrdad

item.title: Doubly Free-Boundary Rail-Yard Dimers and Annular Gaussian Fluctuations
item.description: arXiv:2304.00650v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study rail-yard dimer models with free boundaries at both ends. The double free-boundary geometry introduces infinitely many reflected Cauchy factors into partition functions and contour formulas for height Laplace observables. For admissible piecewise periodic weights satisfying the stated separation conditions, we prove a Laplace-transform law of large numbers and obtain a limit shape through weak convergence of slope measures. For $\beta=1$, under the stated regularity and nonexceptional endpoint conditions, we derive a necessary real double-root condition for the frozen boundary. We also prove Gaussian fluctuations of centered height Laplace observables, with covariance determined by an annular reflected-image kernel expressed through theta functions. Finally, we construct an exact growth-diagram sampler for finite reflected truncations and prove that their laws converge in total variation to the full Gibbs measure on every fixed rail-yard graph with finitely many columns as the truncation level tends to infinity.
item.dc:creator: Zhongyang Li

item.title: A phase transition for the cokernels of random band matrices over the p-adic integers
item.description: arXiv:2408.13037v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathbf{B}_n$ be an $n\times n$ Haar-uniform band matrix over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ with band width $w_n$. We prove that $\text{cok}(\mathbf{B}_n)$ has Cohen-Lenstra limiting distribution if and only if \[\lim_{n\to\infty} \left(w_n-\log_p(n)\right)=+\infty.\]
item.dc:creator: Andr\'as M\'esz\'aros

item.title: Geometry of multidimensional Farey summation algorithm and frieze patterns
item.description: arXiv:2410.13091v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we develop a new geometric approach to subtractive continued fraction algorithms in high dimensions. We adapt a version of Farey summation to the geometric techniques proposed by F. Klein in 1895. More specifically we introduce Farey polyhedra and their sails that generalise respectively Klein polyhedra and their sails, and show similar duality properties of the Farey sail integer invariants. The construction of Farey sails is based on the multidimensional generalisation of the Farey tessellation provided by a modification of the continued fraction algorithm introduced by R. W. J. Meester. We classify Farey polyhedra in the combinatorial terms of prismatic diagrams. Prismatic diagrams extend boat polygons introduced by S. Morier-Genoud and V. Ovsienko in the two-dimensional case. As one of the applications of the new theory we get a multidimensional version of Conway-Coxeter frieze patterns. We show that multidimensional frieze patterns satisfy generalised Ptolemy relations.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Karpenkov, Matty van Son

item.title: On the Depth of Monotone ReLU Neural Networks and ICNNs
item.description: arXiv:2505.06169v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study two models of $\mathsf{ReLU}$ neural networks: monotone networks ($\mathsf{ReLU}^+$) and input convex neural networks ($\mathsf{ICNN}$). Our focus is on expressivity, mostly in terms of depth, and our motivation is to gain a better understanding of the depth required to exactly represent functions using neural networks with ReLU activations, a subject that has received a lot of attention lately. We prove several lower bounds on the depth required to represent functions by monotone ReLU networks and $\mathsf{ICNN}$. For the maximum function $\mathsf{MAX}_n$ computing the maximum of $n$ real numbers, we show that $\mathsf{ReLU}^+$ networks cannot compute $\mathsf{MAX}_n$, or even approximate it. We prove a sharp lower bound of $n-1$ on the $\mathsf{ICNN}$ depth complexity of $\mathsf{MAX}_n$. We also prove depth separations between $\mathsf{ReLU}$ networks and $\mathsf{ICNN}$s; for every $k$, there is a depth-$2$ $\mathsf{ReLU}$ network of size $O(k^2)$ that cannot be simulated by a depth-$k$ $\mathsf{ICNN}$. The proofs are based on deep connections between neural networks and polyhedral geometry, and also use isoperimetric properties of triangulations.
item.dc:creator: Egor Bakaev, Florestan Brunck, Christoph Hertrich, Daniel Reichman, Amir Yehudayoff

item.title: On $q$-real and $q$-complex numbers
item.description: arXiv:2508.08440v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In arXiv:1812.00170 and arXiv:1908.04365, Morier-Genoud and Ovsienko introduced $q$-rational numbers $[x]_q$, rational functions specializing to $x$ at $q=1$, and their extension to $q$-real numbers, Laurent series agreeing with $[x]_q$ for rational $x$. It was conjectured in arXiv:2102.00891 that for every real $x>1$, $[x]_q$ has positive radius of convergence, with optimal common radius $R_*=(3-\sqrt{5})/2$, attained at the golden ratio. We prove that $[x]_q$ converges to a nonvanishing holomorphic function for every real $x>1$ and $|q|<3-2\sqrt{2}$. The proof gives an expansion of $1/[x]_q$ as a $q$-adically convergent series of rational functions, converging absolutely and locally uniformly on an explicit region. It also defines a positive analytic function for $q\in(-R_*,1)$. Using arXiv:2405.15970, we further obtain convergence for $|q|<2-\sqrt{3}$. We compute $[x]_q$ explicitly for some transcendental $x$, including ${\rm cotan}(1)$ and $e$. We also establish sharp inequalities for numerators and denominators of $q$-rationals when $|q|=1$ and determine the closure of the set of $[x]_q$ when such $q$ is not a root of unity. Next, we show that coefficientwise reduction modulo every $m\ge2$ is injective on the Cantor line (the extended real line with doubled up rationals and the Cantor set topology); for $m=2$, it identifies the Cantor line with $\mathbb P^1(\mathbb F_2((q)))$. We describe the inverse map, extend rationality results modulo every prime, characterize quadratic series over $\mathbb F_2(q)$ corresponding to quadratic irrationals, derive criteria for eventual parity of coefficients, and compute the real numbers corresponding to $1+q^n$. Finally, we propose a definition of $q$-complex number $[\tau]_q$, a meromorphic function in $\tau\in\mathbb C_+$ expressed via hypergeometric functions evaluated at modular functions of $\tau$.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Etingof

item.title: Orthogonality of non-pretentious functions to polynomials over Function Fields
item.description: arXiv:2509.12755v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that non-pretentious multiplicative functions are orthogonal to polynomials over function fields (up to characteristic conditions).
item.dc:creator: Tal Meilin

item.title: New Obstacles to Multiple Recurrence
item.description: arXiv:2511.21680v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that there is a set which is not a set of multiple recurrence despite being a set of recurrence for nil-Bohr sets. This answers Huang, Shao, and Ye's "higher-order" version of Katznelson's Question on Bohr recurrence and topological recurrence in the negative. Equivalently, we construct a set $S$ so that there is a finite coloring of $\mathbb{N}$ without monochromatic three-term arithmetic progressions with common differences in $S$, but so that $S$ lacks the usual polynomial obstacles to arithmetic progressions. This represents a significant contribution to our understanding of when a restricted van der Waerden theorem or a restricted Szemer\'edi Theorem holds, an important problem in additive combinatorics and Ramsey theory.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Alweiss

item.title: Discovering hypergeometric series with harmonic numbers via Wilf-Zeilberger seeds
item.description: arXiv:2602.08721v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: By extracting coefficients from Wilf-Zeilberger pairs with respect to auxiliary parameters, we discover many nontrivial hypergeometric series involving harmonic numbers. In particular, we obtain a rapidly convergent series for the depth-two multiple zeta value $\zeta(5,3)$, which appears to be the first result of its kind in the literature. We also investigate the Hilbert series attached to a WZ-seed and conjecture that it admits a remarkably simple form, suggesting the presence of an underlying graded-algebra structure associated with WZ-seeds.
item.dc:creator: Kam Cheong Au

item.title: On rational representations and rational group algebra of $\operatorname{GL}_2(q)$
item.description: arXiv:2606.02415v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article, we study rational representations of $G=\operatorname{GL}_2(q)$, where $q$ is a prime power. Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of $G$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. Then $\rho$ affords the character \[ \Omega(\chi)=m_{\mathbb{Q}}(\chi)\sum_{\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\chi)/\mathbb{Q})}\chi^{\sigma}, \] for some irreducible complex character $\chi$ of $G$, where $m_{\mathbb{Q}}(\chi)$ denotes the Schur index of $\chi$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, and conversely, every character of this form is afforded by an irreducible representation of $G$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. We obtain a combinatorial description for the counting of inequivalent irreducible $\mathbb{Q}$-representations of $G$ of each distinct degree. Furthermore, we briefly determine the rational character table of $G$ and present a method for constructing an irreducible rational matrix representation $\rho$ of $G$ affording the character $\Omega(\chi)$, where $\chi$ is an irreducible complex character of $G$ arising from parabolic induction. Finally, using the results on the rational representations of $G$, we derive an explicit combinatorial formula, depending only on $q$, for the Wedderburn decomposition of $\mathbb{Q}G$.
item.dc:creator: Ram Karan Choudhary, Sunil Kumar Prajapati

item.title: $n$-Centers of Principal Subalgebras $\mathbb K Q_{\geq 1}$ of Path Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2606.23024v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Over a field $\mathbb K$ of characteristic zero, we determine the $St_n$-elements and $n$-centers, defined by standard polynomials, of principal subalgebras of path algebras. Our description expresses each $n$-center as the direct sum of a path ideal and explicit subspaces associated with isolated circles. We prove that these $n$-centers are subalgebras and stabilize for $n\geq2|Q_0|$. We also obtain explicit descriptions of the center and the $3$-center, and determine the least degree of a standard polynomial identity in the acyclic case. Further applications concern algebras of block formal languages and rational Hilbert series of the $n$-centers.
item.dc:creator: Yihao Zheng, Shenglin Zhu

item.title: On the linearity of squarefree powers of edge ideals
item.description: arXiv:2607.00838v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a graph and $I(G)$ its edge ideal. The $p$-th squarefree power $I(G)^{[p]}$ is the monomial ideal generated by the squarefree monomials corresponding to the matchings of size $p$ of $G$. A central highlight of our work is the complete solution of a problem posed by Bigdeli, Herzog and Zaare-Nahandi in 2017, which asked to characterize when squarefree powers of edge ideals have the first syzygy module generated by linear forms. Moreover, for a $1$-dimensional flag simplicial complex $\Delta$ and its Stanley--Reisner ideal $I_\Delta$, which is the edge ideal of the complement graph of $\Delta$, we prove that $I_\Delta^{[p]}$ has a linear resolution if and only if it is linearly related and the $(2p-1)$-st homology of the neighbourhood complex of $\Delta$ vanishes. As a consequence, we describe the shape of the Betti table of $I_\Delta^{[p]}$, and we give a combinatorial characterization of when $I_\Delta^{[p]}$ has a linear resolution, provided that the $2p$-core of $\Delta$ has maximum degree at most $2p$. Finally, we show that no such characterization exists in general: the linearity of $I_\Delta^{[2]}$ may depend on the characteristic of the field, and it cannot be described by finitely many forbidden induced subgraphs.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Navarra, Ayesha Asloob Qureshi, Naoki Terai

item.title: Beyond Mock Modularity: Elliptic Corrections for Higher Dyson Ranks
item.description: arXiv:2607.13159v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When $m = 1$, the Dyson rank generating function is a classical bridge between partition theory, Ramanujan's mock theta functions, and the theory of harmonic Maass forms and nonholomorphic Jacobi forms. The rank is a statistic on partitions, and the higher Dyson systems, for $m \geq 2$, are a natural multivariable refinement of it, combining $m$ graded rank contributions. Unlike the classical case, these higher systems are not expected to fit the mock-modular framework, which raises the question of what analytic structure governs them. We show that their root-of-unity specializations carry a hidden elliptic structure. For $m\ge2$, the primitive $(2m+1)$st-root specialization of their generating function leads to a product deformation whose associated seed satisfies a finite $q$-difference recurrence with an explicit polynomial defect. Using bilateral periodization we construct a meromorphic lift satisfying a twisted index-$m$ elliptic transformation law, with at most simple poles on a prescribed lattice orbit. The poles can be removed by subtracting an explicit multiple of an Appell--Lerch kernel and a specified translation removes the twist. The resulting holomorphic finite parts admit a finite theta decomposition. These results grew out of a human--AI collaboration, and the key new formulas were formalized and machine-verified in Lean/Mathlib by AxiomProver.
item.dc:creator: Claudia Alfes, Ken Ono, Ashvin Swaminathan

item.title: Local Search with Correlated Randomness
item.description: arXiv:2607.17469v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The running-time distribution of a randomized algorithm is computed under independent randomness, but independence is rarely what a source guarantees. We study sources $\nu$ with $\nu[w]\le DP[w]^s$ for every finite prefix $w$ of the tape, where $P$ is an independent reference law, $0<s\le1$, and $D\ge1$; individual choices may be predictable, even determined by the past. The worst-case probability of any closed tape event $E$ is exactly $\min\{1,DC_s(E)\}$, where $C_s(E)$ is the infimum cost of covering $E$ by prefixes of varying depth. This tree max-flow/min-cut identity makes worst-case probabilities exact and optimizable. Three applications follow. In scheduling, $n$ tasks on one machine are each retried until the next random symbol lies in its success set; every schedule has the same makespan distribution under independent randomness, yet under our constraint two fixed orders miss a linear deadline with worst-case probabilities $1$ and $\exp[-\Theta(n)]$, and a static priority rule is optimal at every deadline. For the standard local walk on a $k$-CNF with an assignment satisfying a majority of each clause, we find the sharp source threshold $s_*$: below it, on some instances one admissible source forces nontermination for every clause selection; at it, with fixed $D$, the expected number of flips is at most cubic in the initial distance, against linear under independence, with matching instances at distances up to a constant fraction of the number of variables; a fixed margin above it restores linear dependence. For noisy predecessor search with prefix-bounded comparison errors, verified backtracking attains any prescribed error probability at or above a source threshold whose sharpness we leave open, with the same cubic-to-linear query bounds. Restarting on the shared tape restores exponential tails exactly when the nontermination event has a prefix cover of cost below one.
item.dc:creator: Yunbei Xu

item.title: Leaf-discriminating trees for multiparameter counting of numerical semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2607.23111v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A numerical semigroup is a cofinite additive submonoid of ${\mathbb N}$. The largest element of the complement is its {\em Frobenius number} and the cardinality of its complement is the {\em genus}. We propose a new approach to counting semigroups by the Frobenius number and by the genus, by introducing two ad-hoc trees. Those are leaf-discriminating trees in the sense that their leaves correspond exactly to the objects we want to count and, so, exploring these trees instead of general trees is optimal. Our approach reduces the search space for genus to 23\% and for Frobenius to 0.03\% of that required by previous approaches and this allowed to obtain an important number of unkown terms from both sequences. We implemented a recursive descending algorithm based on the so-called seeds structure, trimming the general semigroup tree exactly at those nodes with no descendants with a given genus, in the first case, or with no descendants with a given Frobenius number, in the second case. We refined the parallelizing strategies and we overcame the previous limitation of the length of integers in the bitwise representation of the gap sequence and the seed sequence. We computed multiparameter decomposition of the numbers of semigroups of each Frobenius number up to $135$, the number of irreducible semigroups of Frobenius number up to $135$, and of the numbers of semigroups of each genus up to $80$.
item.dc:creator: Maria Bras-Amor\'os, Vicen\c{c} Torra

item.title: Sidon sets with $\Delta$-separated sumsets in additive number theory
item.description: arXiv:2608.07416v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The set $A$ is a $B_h$-set if every element of the sumset $hA$ has a unique representation as a sum of $h$ elements of $A$. A $B_2$-set is also called a Sidon set. A $B_{h,\Delta}$-set is a $B_h$-set $A$ whose sumset $hA$ is $\Delta$-separated, that is, $|x-x'| \geq \Delta$ for all $x,x' \in hA$ with $x\neq x'$. Upper and lower bounds are obtained for the cardinality of the largest $B_{2,\Delta}$-sets contained in $\{1,2,\ldots, n\}$, that is, sets $A \subseteq \{1,2,\ldots, n\}$ such that, if $a,b,c,d \in A$ and $\{a,b\} \neq \{c,d\}$, then $|(a+b)-(c+d)| \geq \Delta$.
item.dc:creator: Melvyn B. Nathanson

item.title: A Forced-Structure Reduction and Verifiable Bounds for Conway's 99-Graph
item.description: arXiv:2608.11211v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Conway's 99-graph problem asks whether a strongly regular graph with parameters srg(99,14,1,2) exists. We develop two complementary lines of attack. Fixing one vertex, the conditions lambda=1 and mu=2 force its neighbourhood to be a perfect matching and determine every edge between that neighbourhood and the remaining vertices. For (99,14,1,2), the unresolved part is therefore a constrained 12-regular graph on 84 vertices. We encode this reduction in CP-SAT and validate it by recovering the unique srg(9,4,1,2). We also prove by exhaustive enumeration that no circulant graph on Z/99 satisfies more than 68.0% of the CAISc constraints, and we give a validated orbit formulation for prescribed automorphisms. We then study the partial-score search problem. Fourteen human-designed search configurations reached at most 69.43%. Separately, we supplied the scoring function to an evolutionary program-search system. It produced a degree-preserving 4-vertex-switch tabu search whose best verified artifact scores 70.73%. The generated move differs from those used in our own searches and crosses a plateau that was stable under them. A tabu search restricted to graphs with a prescribed symmetry group, first Z/33 and then its subgroup of order 11, reaches a 14-regular graph scoring 76.67%. These results do not resolve the existence problem, but they reduce the exact search space and improve the best verified partial construction found in our experiments.
item.dc:creator: Aalok Thakkar, Simone Severini

item.title: Limits of Stochastic Semigroups and Block-Triangular Majorisation
item.description: arXiv:2609.04057v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate limits of semigroups of stochastic matrices defined by their invariant distribution. Given probability vectors $q(\beta)$ depending on a parameter $\beta$, we introduce a notion of convergence as $\beta\to\infty$ for the corresponding semigroups of $q(\beta)$-preserving stochastic matrices and investigate the structure of the resulting limit. In general, the limiting semigroup differs from the semigroup preserving the limiting distribution, showing that these two operations do not commute. We develop a general framework for such limiting semigroups and study in detail the case in which the invariant distributions are Gibbs vectors at inverse temperature $\beta$. In that case, the limiting semigroup consists of block-upper-triangular stochastic matrices subject to additional substochasticity constraints. We characterise and enumerate their extremal elements and determine the preorder on probability vectors induced by the action of the semigroup. The resulting notion of Block-Triangular majorisation interpolates between ordinary majorisation and upper triangular (also known as unordered) majorisation. We show that it is completely characterised by a finite family of monotones and analyse the corresponding behaviour of R{\'e}nyi $\alpha$-entropies as $\beta\to\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Fabio Deelan Cunden, Jakub Czartowski, Giovanni Gramegna, Marilena Ligab\`o

item.title: Weighted averages and applications to sets of multiple recurrence
item.description: arXiv:2609.16554v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce new techniques for determining combinatorial properties of sets of multiple recurrence by considering weighted averages with quickly growing weights. Our main result is a far-reaching generalization of Szemer\'edi's Theorem which additionally confirms a conjecture of Bergelson-Moreira-Richter and contains as special cases both a variant of the Polynomial Szemer\'edi Theorem due to Bergelson-Leibman-Lesigne and the fact that if $f$ belongs to a broad class of smooth functions and satisfies $x^{d-1}\prec f(x)\prec x^d$ for some $d\in \mathbb{N}$ then for any $\ell\in \mathbb{N}$, any invertible measure preserving system $(X,\mathscr{B},\mu,T)$, and any $A\in \mathscr{B}$ with $\mu(A)>0$, the set $\{n\in \mathbb{N}: \mu(A\cap T^{-[f(n)]}A\cap T^{-2[f(n)]}A\cap \cdots\cap T^{-\ell[f(n)]}A )>0\}$ is thick, meaning that it contains arbitrarily long intervals of natural numbers. Additionally, we formulate and prove a generalization to weighted averages of Boshernitzan's criterion for uniform distribution which we use in the proof of our main result.
item.dc:creator: Vitaly Bergelson, Michael Reilly

item.title: Polyhedral Methods for Cooperative Games: Small Lifts and Hard Faces
item.description: arXiv:2609.24593v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the computational complexity of fundamental algorithmic problems -- membership testing, separation, valid-inequality testing, and linear optimization -- over polytopes and cones arising from cooperative games (also known as pseudo-Boolean functions). A central obstacle in the study of such problems is that a general cooperative game on $n$ players requires $2^n$ values, so the input size is $2^n$ for a game with $n$ players, making these computational tasks theoretically trivial. Restricting to $k$-additive games reduces the input size to $O(n^k)$, making such games a natural target for meaningful questions about the existence of efficient algorithms. On the positive side, we give an explicit extended formulation of size $O(n^k)$ for the core of $k$-additive $k$-monotone games, allowing all four problems to be solved by a single polynomial-size linear program -- in particular, circumventing the ellipsoid method that is needed when building from earlier tractability results of Deng and Papadimitriou, or of Edmonds. For the cone of $k$-additive $(k{-}1)$-monotone games, we give a complete characterization of its extreme rays and derive the same $O(n^k)$ bound on extension complexity, yielding a geometry-based proof and generalization of a result of Billionnet and Minoux. On the negative side, we show that for $l \leq k-2$ the cone of $k$-additive $l$-monotone games is computationally intractable: membership testing is not in NP (unless NP\,=\,coNP), valid-inequality testing is NP-complete, and extension complexity is at least $1.5^n$. Our hardness results yield, as a special case, a result of Crama and of Gallo and Simone. Furthermore, our hardness results also explain the lack of any good characterization of the extreme rays of the cone of $k$-additive $(k{-}2)$-monotone games.
item.dc:creator: Michel Grabisch and. Hans Raj Tiwary

item.title: Maximal Linear Arrangement is NP complete on Bipartite Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.12613v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The linear arrangement of a simple graph $G = (V,E)$ is a bijective labeling $\pi$ of the vertices of $G$ to the set $\{1, \ldots, n\}$. The maximum linear arrangement ($\texttt{maxLA}$) problem is to determine whether $G$ has a labeling such that the sum of labels across $G$'s edges, $\sum_{uv \in E} |\pi(u) - \pi(v)|$, is at least a given value $k$. Minimum linear arrangement ($\texttt{minLA}$) is defined analogously. Both $\texttt{maxLA}$ and $\texttt{minLA}$ are known to be NP complete for general graphs. $\texttt{minLA}$ has shown to be NP complete for bipartite graphs by Evans and Shiloah in 1975. It has been an open problem whether the same holds for $\texttt{maxLA}$. In this paper we prove that $\texttt{maxLA}$ is NP complete for bipartite graphs.
item.dc:creator: Aparna Das, Jonathan Needleman

item.title: Perron--Wright asymptotics and critical component processes for inhomogeneous random graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.23003v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend Wright's enumeration of connected labelled graphs with fixed surplus to irreducible critical finite type kernels and continuous compact type kernels satisfying a positivity condition. Let $\mathsf{C}_t(k,r)$ denote the total weight of connected labelled graphs with $k$ vertices and surplus $r$. Let $u>0$ satisfy $Ku=u$ and $\int u d\mu=1$, and put $\alpha=\int u^2 d\mu$ and $\beta=\int u^3 d\mu$. We prove that the rooted-tree radius $\rho$ is positive and real analytic near $1$, with $\rho(1)=1$ and $\log\rho(t)=\frac{\alpha^2}{2\beta}(t-1)^2+O(|t-1|^3)$, and that, for fixed $r\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ and $0\le L<\infty$, $\mathsf{C}_t(k,r)=w_r\beta^{(r-1)/2}e^{-k}\rho(t)^{-k}k^{k+3r/2-2}\{1+O_{r,L}(k^{-1/2})\}$, uniformly for $|t-1|\le Lk^{-1/2}$, where $w_r$ is the classical Wright constant. At criticality, the leading constant depends on the kernel only through $\beta$, under the stated normalization of $u$. At $t_n=1+\lambda n^{-1/3}$, exact component identities combine with these asymptotics to give fixed size factorial densities and local size and surplus point-process limits for deterministic finite type models and annealed compact type Bollob\'as-Janson-Riordan models. With sizes rescaled by $\beta^{1/3}n^{-2/3}$, the limit is the Aldous process at parameter $\alpha\beta^{-2/3}\lambda$, and the corresponding type profiles concentrate at the Perron law $p(dx)=u(x)\mu(dx)$. For every bounded uniformly positive countable critical kernel, we construct graph sequences with growing finite supports and the same local limits, and identify the additive shift of the critical window caused by spectral perturbations of order $n^{-1/3}$.
item.dc:creator: Wentao Hu, Wen Sun

item.title: Webs and exponentially large mu-coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.34982v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using webs, we prove that Kazhdan-Lusztig mu-coefficients for symmetric groups grow at least exponentially with the rank, already for pairs labeled by a three-row rectangle.
item.dc:creator: Tom Goertzen, Abel Lacabanne, Daniel Tubbenhauer, Pedro Vaz

item.title: Exchange graphs and $\tau$-tilting complexes of surface rigid algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.41703v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We classify the connected components of support $\tau$-tilting graphs of surface rigid algebras associated with partial tagged triangulations of punctured marked surfaces with nonempty boundary. For a connected algebra, the graph is disconnected precisely when the algebra is weakly symmetric, has at least two simple modules and has Cartan rank one. There are then exactly two components. The completion graph of every nonzero $\tau$-rigid pair over a connected surface rigid algebra is connected. Suppose the defining partial tagged triangulation is nonempty and all its endpoints are punctures. Then the realization of the support $\tau$-tilting complex is homotopy equivalent to a sphere of dimension $\operatorname{rank}C_A-1$. Signed endpoint vectors give an explicit homotopy equivalence. Under the same endpoint hypothesis, $\tau$-tilting finiteness is equivalent to positive definiteness of the Cartan matrix. In the finite case, we determine the primitive $g$-vector ray generators in endpoint coordinates and give a surface criterion distinguishing the root sets of types $A$, $D$ and $C$. The homotopy construction also applies to Brauer graph algebras with arbitrary vertex multiplicities.
item.dc:creator: Ping He, Bo Le
